#126. Beto O’Rourke Says He’d “Do Anything” for James Talarico and Gina Hinojosa—Including Work for Them

📅 12 Nov 2026

Beto O’Rourke Says He’d “Do Anything” for James Talarico and Gina Hinojosa—Including Work for Them

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.vanityfair.com/story/beto-orourke-texas-interview

Berdasarkan laporan, after the shocking democratic victories in texas last week, it was hard not to look over the shoulders of james talarico and gina hinojosa and see the shadow of beto o’rourke, whose losses for senate in 2018 and governor in 2022 had become cautionary tales of democratic hopelessness in texas. And perhaps proof that nice guys couldn’t win. But in the years after those failed runs, O’Rourke never really went away. He launched a voter-registration group called Powered by People, punched out missives on Substack, livestreamed his thoughts, and quietly advised his party from the background.

Diungkapkan bahwa “should i have talked to joe hagan when he was on my front porch in 2019?” o’rourke says now, looking back at the cover story i wrote, in which he proclaimed he was “just born to be in it,” a premature declaration that almost immediately sank his prospects. “I’m glad I did. I’m grateful for everything that’s happened, because look where we are. It’s a beautiful new day in America. ”.

O'Rourke taks the stage during the Fight the Trump Takeover rally at the Texas Capitol in August 2025.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, like stacey abrams in georgia, who lost her own race for governor but used her visibility to build a stronger coalition, o’rourke can claim some credit for setting the table for democratic success in texas. ” When he launched his Senate campaign, Talarico said he wanted to replicate O’Rourke’s “energy. When Talarico asked whether he’d run, O’Rourke said only if Talarico ran for governor instead, eventually stepping aside after concluding that the moment called for “something and someone new. And as it turns out, O’Rourke himself weighed another Senate run this year. Talarico won his first race, for a Republican-held state House seat, on O’Rourke’s 2018 wave. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, o’rourke, meanwhile, became a behind-the-scenes player: powered by people was one of four partners in the texas democrats’ $30 million coordinated campaign, and it says it reached more than 110,000 new and young voters in texas this cycle. Ken Paxton noticed and tried to put O’Rourke “behind bars” for funding the Democrats who fled the state to block its Donald Trump–backed redistricting.

Sebagaimana diketahui, o’rourke says the wave cascaded so far down the ballot in texas that a candidate who tried backing out of her campaign before election day ended up winning. “At that point it was too late to take her name off the ballot,” he says. That speaks to the magnitude of the wave, but also to the value of having a fighter on every front. “She didn’t campaign, just won her election. Somebody said to me, ‘A wave’s great, even better if you have a surfboard. ’”.

Over an hour-long conversation, O’Rourke parses the political revolution in his home state, suggests how Democrats can hold on to their land grab, and, perhaps unsurprisingly, looks ahead to another run for office.

This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

Diungkapkan bahwa vanity fair: the conventional wisdom is that this was a revolt against trump, and that the candidates and the democratic strategy were secondary. What’s your read?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, beto o’rourke: so much of this election was a rejection of trump and trumpism: the corruption, the wars, the cruelty. President Obama, I think wisely, held back…. Kamala Harris turned out not to be it. But after 2024, people were anxious that we didn’t have a unifying national leader. [Joe] Biden was not going to be it. Chuck Schumer was persona non grata in any gathering of Democrats. The DNC was in the red.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, what it did was allow for candidates in different parts of the country to really establish themselves in their own right and by their own merits, never having to fear being under the shadow of a larger figure. That’s how you get Abdul El-Sayed, James Talarico, Mary Peltola, all these extraordinary candidates who are extraordinarily different from each other. It’s really a blessing. In Texas, for the first time in half a century, Democrats fielded a fighter on every front: 150 state House candidates, 38 congressional candidates, 16 state Senate candidates. You had to have a historically terrible, corrupt president. But you also had to have this historically beaten-down Democratic Party; that the Democrats don’t have a message, they don’t have a leader. That all turned out to be a great thing.

Read Party Animals: A letter from the back rooms, barstools, and bacchanals of Washington, DC—with exclusive reporting, interviews, and analysis.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, a year ago you convened talarico, colin allred, and joaquin castro to think about a statewide slate. Talarico went his own way. You warned him he’d “want friends on that ticket. ” What did you mean?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i just wanted to win, and i put that before anything else. James and I had many conversations before he officially announced. He asked me, “Are you interested? Would you run?” And I told him, “The only condition on which I would run is if you were to run for governor, or somebody else who could draw that kind of attention and resources, and if we had the ticket rounded out by strong contenders for every position on the ballot. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, my advice to him was: “look, i’ve done this before. No matter how talented you are, no matter how much you can raise, this state is so big, the Republicans are so entrenched, you need a fighter on every front. Gina really hit her stride at the right time. ” And ultimately, that’s what happened. Her strength as a candidate a year ago compared to how she finished is worlds apart, and that is a testament to what an exceptional leader she is.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, clearly, it was the right call for james to be there. He was absolutely the right guy for the moment. He was a phenomenally focused candidate. I know from being on college campuses how electrifying she is, how many young people she brought into the electorate this time. He is just an extraordinarily talented communicator. I also think it was the right call for Jasmine Crockett to run too. They stayed in even after Jasmine was defeated in the primary.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the atlantic reported that you told hinojosa, “not one person can win texas. It has to be two. ” Is that what you said?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i definitely spoke to gina before she made the decision to run, and then after. That was based on the last run I had, in 2022, and even the ’18 run. ” What I said consistently to everybody who was thinking about it—Colin, Joaquin, Gina, Jasmine [Crockett], James—was that you need a fighter on every front and the strongest possible ticket. To be honest with you, I can’t remember if I said “two. If Joaquin or Julián Castro had run for governor when I was running for Senate, who knows? Of course, at that time, we didn’t know the size of the wave that was about to crash.

Diungkapkan bahwa i definitely did. You’d have to ask James, but I think he probably would have supported that if I had. We have an amazing organization in waiting, volunteers who’ve been with me, the ability to raise money. I could have run…. But was that the right thing to do? No. I had been before Texas twice before, and the moment demanded something different and, I would argue, something better.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, you can’t discount a politician’s ambition and ego. I don’t know that Texas could have produced a stronger—I was going to say candidate, but really a one-two punch. My love language is a town hall meeting, where it’s just a free-for-all and anybody can step to the mic and ask any questions. Also, I spent a lot of time traveling Texas. It helped having conversations with our kids. It helped having conversations with people who’d been on these runs with me before. It helped having conversations with my wife. At the end of that, I really felt this moment called for something and someone new. They’re both exceptional individually. It was James and Gina. I had to find a way to get past that. Together, they transcended what had happened in politics for as long as I’ve been alive.

Sebagaimana diketahui, honestly, my own doubt about whether texas could be won was based on you. We’d seen this story before.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i wouldn’t have done this work as a volunteer for the last four years if i didn’t believe in texas. I know in my heart and in my bones that we are so much better than the people in power. It’s insane having Texas Republicans say, if you’re Muslim, regardless of whether you’re an immigrant, you should be deported from this country. It’s the obscene abortion ban that has cost the lives of girls and women, the $7. Four years after Uvalde, and no one in power has done a single thing. 25-an-hour minimum wage, the fact that we’re the least insured state in the country. That’s just not who we are.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, o'rourke speaks during the fight the trump takeover rally, where 5,000 people attended. Attendees protested proposed redistricting, immigration enforcement, and other Trump-backed legislation and proposed changes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when i ran for governor, 9 million registered voters didn’t cast a ballot. This state makes it harder than any other to participate, so we’ve got to try that much harder. But did I know it would be 2026? Did I know it would be every statewide office and the state House? Fuck no, man. I knew it was a matter of time and effort. It’s not because they don’t care; it’s not that they’re lazy. The greater the effort, the shorter the time. Nobody knew that.

Diungkapkan bahwa ken paxton called you a “repeat loser” and tried to prosecute your pac. He lost by 12 points.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we’ve spent more than $600,000; we have powered by people defending our organization, defending me. He promised to lock me up, to put me behind bars. The 15th Court of Appeals [judges], all of whom were appointed by Greg Abbott, so none of them friends of mine, have ruled against Paxton for attacking somebody for exercising their First Amendment rights. He tried to remove the license for Powered by People to do voter-registration work in the state of Texas. He accused me of bribery. Do I think that I’m going to get that money back? I don’t know.

Couldn’t have happened to a better person.

Did Talarico and Hinojosa acknowledge your role, or did they keep their distance?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, you’d have to ask them. That’s not an easy choice for Gina, right? Both of them did an exceptional job of being themselves and not seeming to be beholden to anybody. They invited nobody in from outside of Texas, and we all understood: This is their show. I got a really nice message from James on election night, and I had a chance to campaign with Gina in the closing days of the election. So getting to campaign with Gina here at the University of Texas at El Paso, at the University of Houston, it was really nice to hear her acknowledge the work that so many of us have been doing, especially all these volunteers who’ve been out there, whose names most people will never know.

Berdasarkan laporan, i’ve known them both for a decade. These are really fucking good human beings, and they’re also really good at understanding power and how to win it. James and I were on the campaign trail together in 2017 and 2018, when he was running his first race for state House in Williamson County. Somebody just sent me a picture of the two of us at an event in Williamson in 2017. It is so rare that those two things come together.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, o'rourke speaks during a "fighting oligarchy" event in houston, texas on oct. 20, 2026.

Are Chuck Schumer and Hakeem Jeffries the right leaders for this moment?.

Berdasarkan laporan, chuck schumer absolutely is not. They’re all bending the knee—the Ivy Leagues, the big law firms, the media companies. Hakeem marshaled every Democratic vote in the House but one to stop Trump, DOGE, and Musk, and the deal with Schumer was going to do the same. Then, inexplicably, Schumer bent the knee as well. Early 2025, [Elon] Musk is running wild with DOGE, Trump is steamrolling every center of power. In that moment, it was absolutely over for me.

Sebagaimana diketahui, schumer deserves so much credit and praise for his work over the decades. The age when any American cares what the majority leader reads on the Senate floor is over. But he doesn’t deserve to be majority leader at this major turning point for the country, not when you have James Talarico, Abdul El-Sayed, or Jon Ossoff. We have an embarrassment of talent in the Senate right now, and we should use it. I don’t even know what his message is, and that says something.

Sebagaimana diketahui, hakeem jeffries hasn’t had the chance to lead as speaker. We were elected in the same class in 2012, and I’m grateful that he stood strong early in the Trump administration. I wish he could communicate more effectively than he has so far. Maybe there’s a scenario where he’s Speaker, but he taps the far better communicators in his caucus, like Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, to do more of that work, and he’s focused on getting the legislative results.

Berdasarkan laporan, eleven house democrats missed the vote to impeach [pete] hegseth, enough to have changed the outcome. What happened there?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, eleven is a big number. That certainly invites some conspiracy thinking, or, maybe just as bad, the idea that these folks aren’t up to the job. It’s really important that the Democratic leadership in the House address this directly, explain what happened, and take ownership and responsibility for it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, you’ve said democrats wasted their power in 2009 and 2021, and that next time they should “drive that car like we stole it. ” What happens in the first 100 days?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, right off the bat, you have to make our lives better in a way that we can feel. Raise the minimum wage from $7. 25. In Texas, that’s not hard, because we are in such a fucking hole. Expand Medicaid when the federal government’s paying 90 cents on the dollar. Stop this voucher thing that is draining tax dollars from local schools, and pay teachers so they don’t have to work a second or third job.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, nationally, you have to do the same. Maybe there are deals to be had. I don’t think there’s someone who reads power better than he does. I don’t like anything about him, but I don’t know that there’s a more successful political operator than Trump. The response to this from many is that Trump has the power of the pen and will veto that. Maybe you force the veto, and you set up a clear contrast going into 2028. Make him veto that. At a minimum, you have to get caught trying.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the huge issues that democrats have absolutely failed to lead on, we have to lead on now, so that would include immigration and that would include democracy. [Pushing] the popular-vote compact; I think we have enough trifectas now. There is a democracy you can build anew. People give a speech and are like, “We’ve got to overturn Citizens United,” or, “We’ve got to do away with the Electoral College. Getting a voting rights act passed again. Getting corporations out of politics; what just passed in Montana is potentially a wonderful precedent from which we could build. [On democracy], there’s no democracy to restore or save. I’m probably in the minority in the Democratic Party, but I’m a big believer in term limits. Immigration was arguably the issue that voters made their decisions on in 2016 and 2024, and if we continue to hope that it’s just going to solve itself, instead of making tough choices and using political capital on this, then it’s going to be our demise in future elections as well. ” That’s a great applause line, but when is that ever going to happen?.

O'Rourke spoke in October 2026 as the fight for the Senate came down to the wire.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the big dig on democrats is: you talked a great game on immigration, then you won the white house; you had the house and the senate. You didn’t do anything. You talked a great game about voting rights. You had the trifecta, and you didn’t do anything. Now we have the power. We’d better deliver, or watch out.

Berdasarkan laporan, i’m surprised i’m not hearing more from you about prosecutions and subpoenas. You spent the last two years warning about fascism and calling for accountability.

Diungkapkan bahwa that’s got to be part of it too. The law is king in this country; no one’s above it, no one’s below it. I spent a lot of time with young people doing this voter-registration work, and that is probably the number one thing I hear from them for why they don’t vote: This shit doesn’t work. We’ve allowed the precedent, through the Epstein crimes, that you can be rich enough and well-connected enough to rape and traffic girls and women with complete impunity. Ghislaine Maxwell [went to jail], but no man who actually did this has gone to prison or even faced trial.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, then there’s the corruption that flows from the president through his family, through his cabinet officials, through the oligarchs [with whom] he surrounds himself. Look at the Roman Republic. It wasn’t Caesar crossing the Rubicon. I know this is an unpopular thing to talk about within our party, because folks want to turn the page. It was Sulla turning his armies against Rome, and there was never a consequence or accountability for that, so the precedent was set and Caesar picked that up. If we let this stand, much the way that we let stand his crimes against this country on January 6, 2021, that sets the most dangerous precedent. [Editor’s note: O’Rourke is an avid fan of the podcast The Rest Is History. But that keeps biting us in the ass. ] There will be a more capable, powerful demagogue than Trump—he or she may be a Democrat; he or she may be a Republican—who will use that precedent unless that door is closed. Everyone who went to prison for [January 6] was pardoned by this president.

But if you spend the next two years investigating him and prices stay high, Democrats are cooked.

Berdasarkan laporan, that’s exactly right. Democrats are responsible for so many good things that are both slow-working and expressed through the tax code, like the child tax credit, and for which they don’t claim credit. That’s why I said you’ve got to deliver for people, and they have to feel it immediately. Those things have to change.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i was in the rio grande valley after 2020, doing voter registration, knocking on doors, and talking to this guy who voted for trump. I said, “You had a front-row seat to kids in cages, to family separation, to this cruelty here. I don’t have that luxury. ” We have to learn that lesson. And now that they are pursuing these investigations and this accountability, I trust them, and I know that, regardless of the outcome of these investigations, my life is better because they are in power. Tell me what’s going on. ” And he said, “I hate all that stuff, but voting on those issues when I can’t feed my family and I may lose my home is a luxury. They really reflect my values and my interests. You’ve got to make people’s lives better, and if you do that, you build trust and legitimacy: “Okay, these guys are really helping me. ”.

If Trump felt that he or his family were under real legal threat, is there any world in which investigations become a chip to trade, say, for immigration reform? I realize this is very Trumpy thinking, but you are dealing with Trump.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, no. They lied to us, they lied to the world, and it took the lives of so many Americans, Iraqis, and Afghans. Totally understandable, and it’s a recognition of how politics and power typically work. But part of how we got Trump in the first place was that there weren’t consequences for massive failures or crimes committed: these banks that were bailed out after they had driven so many Americans into poverty and homelessness in 2008 and 2009, these wars the Bush administration launched on false pretenses. Never any consequence or accountability.

Berdasarkan laporan, this corruption has been so flagrant, it’s as though trump and those closest to him were daring america to hold them accountable. But if there’s accountability, then that becomes the precedent upon which future leaders will be able to act. Then there’s the open defiance of the law and the Constitution: killing people on fishing boats in the Caribbean, kidnapping a head of state, launching a war and continuing it in violation of the War Powers Act. When you allow these things to stand, they become the precedent. Trump may feel he’s fighting for his life, that he’s backed into a corner. He may make it harder for Democrats to do the things that they need to do. But I don’t think we can operate in fear of him.

Berdasarkan laporan, some democrats, like alexandria ocasio-cortez, argue that the corruption and the high prices are the same story. Do you buy that?.

Diungkapkan bahwa talarico is masterful at saying that: their corruption is costing you and your family. Billionaires bought off Governor Greg Abbott and persuaded him to pursue a voucher scheme that took public dollars out of local schools and sent them to private schools, decreased the quality of your school, and raised your local property taxes to make up the difference. So many examples in Texas. Abbott, beholden to corporate interests, opened the door [to data centers], and our electricity prices went up and the quality of our water and air was compromised.

O'Rourke says he doesn't know if there’s an office he can imagine running for in 2028 or 2030.

Diungkapkan bahwa the biggest one was in 2021, when we had the winter storm. One of the pipeline operator CEOs wrote Abbott a $1 million check at the end of that winter storm, almost as if to say thank you for not prosecuting them. It’s not corruption in an abstract way; it’s corruption that’s costing you. And yes, that corruption should be prosecuted. It’s not enough to just win the election and throw the bums out. In the energy capital of the world, they couldn’t keep the lights on or the power running, and pipeline operators [and others in the energy industry], among the biggest donors to Greg Abbott, began to price-gouge, bankrupting utilities and causing ratepayers to pay sky-high prices. If the bums broke the law, then they have to face the consequences.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if democrats hold this ground, it would seem to open the door for you again. Is there an office you can imagine running for in 2028 or 2030?.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i don’t know, and people would have to answer that question for me. That’s what I’ve been trying to do these last four years, just listen to people and figure out where I can be most useful. I’ve tried to remain agnostic.

Berdasarkan laporan, i had a conversation earlier in the year with somebody who just won in texas, and they had been one of the people to encourage me to run for governor in 2022—what the fuck was i thinking, running in joe biden’s midterm?—and i asked them, “did you think i had any chance to win?” and they said, “oh god, no. ” But they knew that we needed somebody to galvanize the state, protect our gains in Harris County, and shore up the wins that we’d [earned] in 2018. Somebody had to carry us through that next stage of the relay.

Sebagaimana diketahui, just so i’m clear, i would not have run if i didn’t think there was a chance we could win in 2022. It was an incredibly tough environment that got tougher and tougher as the race proceeded. But it did a lot of good, and in some small way it was probably helpful toward what happened in 2026.

Diungkapkan bahwa when [my wife] amy and i made the decision in 2016 that we had to do something, i went to everyone: joaquin and julián castro, clay jenkins, michael sorrell, wendy davis. ” Ultimately, I was like, “Okay, if you guys aren’t going to do it, I am going to do it. I know this is crazy, and I know all of you are better positioned, I’m going to do it. ” So if I feel the way that I felt that time, that I’m the right person for this, then, whatever the odds, I’m going to get out there. I asked each of them, “Will you run? If you do, I will get behind you. But if running could hurt us, if there’s somebody better—and that was a conclusion I drew coming into this cycle—then please step up, and I’ll get out of the way and support you as a volunteer.

Diungkapkan bahwa the next statewide race in texas is 2030. I’m happy to follow James and Gina’s lead. I want to be part of the team getting Texas ready for that nominee to win our state. One thing I’m thinking about right now is 2028, and the fact that the 40 Electoral College votes in Texas are ours to lose. They’re our leaders now.

Can you imagine working in a Hinojosa administration?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i will do anything for her, and the same for james. It’s just crazy, hearing that.

What about taking Powered by People to Florida? They could use some help, evidently.

Diungkapkan bahwa these states of the former confederacy have worked so hard to make it hard for people, especially young people, to vote. We could have won those races. 3%. Heartbreaking. We don’t have Election Day data yet, but through early voting, 60% of our voters, overwhelmingly 18 to 29 years old, voted through early voting. That’s about 33 points ahead of the average for that demographic in Texas. What was [the margin] in the governor’s race? 1. I sure wish our party had put resources behind [Angie] Nixon and [David] Jolly in Florida. If I can be useful there, I’m happy to go.

Berdasarkan laporan, about a year after my 2019 story came out, i texted you that i hoped there were no hard feelings, and you took responsibility for your own errors. It seems like you’ve been through a process since then.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, that’s just life, right? i truly feel so incredibly lucky: getting to serve in congress, getting to run for the us senate, being considered for the nomination in 2020, being back out on the trail for governor, and then doing this work with powered by people. I’m grateful for everything that’s happened, because look at where we are. Then I’m prone to feel sorry for myself or to wonder what if. So I try not to dwell too much on decisions that I’ve made. #132. The Lord Of The Rings: The Rings Of Power Season 3: The Secret Fire Explained

📅 12 Nov 2026

The Lord Of The Rings: The Rings Of Power Season 3: The Secret Fire Explained

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2315290/the-lord-of-the-rings-the-ring-f-power-season-3-secret-fire-explained/

Diungkapkan bahwa you cannot pass! the dark fire will not avail you, flame of spoilers for "the rings of power" season 3, episode 3, "the secret fire. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the rings of power" season 3 does a lot of things right, especially when sauron is on screen attempting to make a shiny piece of jewelry to master all other pieces of jewelry — all while being haunted by the ghost of celebrimbor. Indeed, the show shines most when it focuses on the bad guys, like introducing the stunning-looking Nazgnagôl or Adam Young's orc with shifting loyalties and a penchant for poetry.

Berdasarkan laporan, one thing that is different this season is the lack of mystery identities. D. We now know very well who Sauron is, we know that The Stranger is actually Gandalf, we finally learn this season who the Dark Wizard is, and we even know why Theo is still in this story. It's as if "The Rings of Power" creators J. Payne and Patrick McKay got tired of the waiting around and decided to have god himself come down and explain things directly at the audience.

Diungkapkan bahwa well, that is actually exactly what happens in episode 3, because gandalf (daniel weyman) has an actual burning bush moment and talks to the actual god of j. R. R. Tolkien's Legendarium to learn about the Secret Fire, and his purpose in the story.

Berdasarkan laporan, in the episode, tom bombadil (rory kinnear) sends gandalf on a quest to chase a rabbit. This leads Gandalf to an altar where the rabbit combusts into a flame that speaks to the wizard and explains he is the almighty, whose Secret Fire burns inside every creature on Middle-earth.

Berdasarkan laporan, even though "the rings of power" is set in a world of magic rings, dragons, dwarves and elves, we have not really seen a lot of thel supernatural — despite it being relatively common in middle-earth. R. R. The world of J. Tolkien is one of angels and elves that get resurrected, a world that literally goes from flat to round when the creator of all existence gets angry at men and sinks an entire continent to the bottom of the sea.

Sebagaimana diketahui, this is the most overt example of supernatural fantasy we've got in "the rings of power" so far, as gandalf hears a strange voice (allan corduner) coming from a manifestation of a flame. The flame gives Gandalf (after calling him by his original Quenya name Olórin) a cosmic vision as the voice reveals itself to be the one who "built the heavens and the stars," that which burns within all living things. As the voice says, "all of Middle-earth is cradled within my flame. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, that is the secret fire, which is alluded to by gandalf in the original "lord of the rings" trilogy. The Secret Fire, or Flame Imperishable, is Gandalf's higher calling, essentially the power of Tolkien's equivalent of God. That fire is inside all living beings, and is the thing Morgoth craved most, because he was unable to create life without it, the reason he was driven to the shadow. Named Erū Ilúvatar, this being is the creator of the whole world, and his Secret Fire is what gives life to the universe. In Tolkien's world, the Secret Fire is the equivalent of the Holy Spirit in Abrahamic religions, the manifestation of the almighty within all beings.

Berdasarkan laporan, it is quite funny that "the rings of power" has arguably its biggest exposition dump of season 3 come directly from god, who reveals to gandalf the entire history of the istari and reveals the identity of the dark wizard. After 2 seasons of audiences trying to work out the identity of the Dark Wizard and his purpose, along drops god from the heavens and just outright explains that he is actually a Blue Wizard and gives audiences the whole backstory in a single scene.

Sebagaimana diketahui, of course, as shocking as erū ilúvatar appearing in "the rings of power" is, it makes sense for the show to introduce him now. That's because he has a big role to play in Season 4 and the fall of Númenor. Still, the idea that this show has now officially involved higher beings in the conflict against Sauron is a deep cut concept that separates this from other fantasy shows.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, in tolkien's text, the valar (essentially the gods of olympus under erū ilúvatar's zeus) don't get directly involved in the wars of middle-earth (at least not since elrond's father convinced the valar to physically aid in the fight against morgoth), but their influence and power is felt all throughout the second age of middle-earth and the war against sauron. "The Rings of Power" leaning more into the supernatural fantasy of Tolkien is one way of making this already quite expansive world even more interesting and complex.

#142. Ebenezer Review: Johnny Depp Neither Helps Nor Hurts This Passionless Retelling

📅 12 Nov 2026

Ebenezer Review: Johnny Depp Neither Helps Nor Hurts This Passionless Retelling

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2314564/ebenezer-review-johnny-depp-a-christmas-carol-movie/

Berdasarkan laporan, charles dickens' 1843 novella "a christmas carol" is one of the greatest stories ever written. It's a tale that is both very much of its time as well as timeless, speaking to systemic issues of cold-hearted greed and inequality as well as the ability to change one's ways for the better. It's a malleable text that can be calibrated for all ages, just as it can be told with everything from a lighthearted touch to a more dour and sinister horror-centric one.

Diungkapkan bahwa this versatility has led it to become one of the most commonly adapted stories of all time. To put it mildly, we are not lacking for versions of Dickens' "Christmas Carol. " That doesn't mean further adaptations shouldn't be made, but rather that the artists behind them should have a unique take on the material; like Shakespeare, it's well known enough to not have to play completely straight.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, yet playing it straight seems to be the entire ethos for "ebenezer," the new adaptation from director ti west and starring johnny depp as scrooge. That seems to be what West and company are assuming with Depp in the role, and it's likely why the rest of the film around him isn't taking too many big swings. Scott have done. Yet it leaves "Ebenezer" feeling a little too plain on the one hand, and potentially unsavory where Depp's personal status is considered. If a "Christmas Carol" adaptation isn't taking a big swerve with either a singing Will Ferrell or Muppets, for example, the general assumption is that some renowned actor will give their take on Scrooge, as luminaries like Alastair Sim, Albert Finney, and George C. It's a movie that seems to exist on Depp's shoulders for better or worse, a choice that leaves it being technically competent but ultimately confused.

Diungkapkan bahwa if you already know "a christmas carol," then "ebenezer" will not hold many surprises for you. Ti West and screenwriter Nathaniel Halpern treat Charles Dickens' novella in much the same way the Royal Shakespeare Company might treat "Hamlet," which is to say that they retain the bulk of Dickens' dialogue and structure (the film is even separated into five staves, as in the novella) while coloring outside the lines ever so often. After an original opening sequence detailing the literal end of the partnership between Marley (Ian McKellen) and Ebenezer Scrooge (Johnny Depp), the film chronicles the usual beats of the tale, from establishing Scrooge's miserly, calloused attitude to the gradual thawing of his soul via his haunting by three Christmas ghosts.

Although Paramount Pictures' ghastly marketing campaign promised that "Ebenezer" would present a Scrooge we'd never seen before and go places other adaptations hadn't dared, the true extent of any changes or embellishments to the Dickens tale lies in the way that certain very small supporting characters who purport to either be in service of the needy or in need themselves are revealed to be greedy con artists.

Berdasarkan laporan, the choice does add a nice little layer of moral complexity to what is typically a straightforward story, yet west and company don't do all that much with it in the end. Given his extensive indie horror background, West does lend the proceedings a welcome macabre aesthetic. The three ghosts are especially ghastly and eerie, and the whole film has a Victorian London by way of '70s British films feel to it, like if Ronald Neame's "Scrooge" was mashed up with West's "The Innkeepers. This is certainly the spookiest "Christmas Carol" since Robert Zemeckis' bizarre 2006 version. ".

Sebagaimana diketahui, while much of "ebenezer" is solid and skillfully crafted, it's all clearly in service of the character and the performer at its center. To say that Johnny Depp brings some baggage to the role is to make an understatement, for even setting aside the considerable issue of his offscreen life, his onscreen persona would be its own monolith to reckon with. Especially in this material, as it blatantly conjures up his past successes with director Tim Burton.

Diungkapkan bahwa what made the depp/burton duo special was how the director was able to draw out some truly bizarre character choices from the actor while making sure the film around him fit the outrageous, heightened tone of the performance. Here in "Ebenezer," Depp appears to be shooting more for respectable prestige than crowd-pleasing outrageousness. He's not trying to pull a Jack Sparrow, in other words, and instead is letting the prosthetic makeup do much of the transformation for him.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, with the exception of a small moment here and there, depp's scrooge is largely solid yet unremarkable. It's possible that Depp now considers such an approach something he's no longer interested in, and it's not like he hasn't given grounded performances before, like his turn as John Dillinger in "Public Enemies," for example. Which begs the question: why bother in the first place? It seems like the entirety of "Ebenezer" was arranged to allow Depp to chew scenery and showboat around, which the actor perversely refuses to do. Depp's performance as Scrooge simply doesn't feel fully realized. It's fine on paper, and even has flashes of depth, yet it ultimately is more calibrated than inspired.

Berdasarkan laporan, i have a deep affection for "a christmas carol," and generally find something to like in all of its many adaptations. Ti West, Nathaniel Halpern, Depp and the rest haven't twisted the story beyond recognition, nor have they sullied it. In this way, "Ebenezer" is no different. Yet in playing things so generally safe, "Ebenezer" becomes a muted film.

Sebagaimana diketahui, west throws in a flourish here and there, like the great work with the three ghost characters or a moment where scrooge is abducted through his bed that deliberately recalls depp's cinematic debut in "a nightmare on elm street. " There's even an extended denouement to the tale which stands in contrast to most versions of "A Christmas Carol," where instead of rushing through Scrooge's change of heart, the film takes its time as the man makes his reparations.

Sebagaimana diketahui, yet even that choice feels calculated in a meta sense to better present johnny depp, movie star, back to the public after his cancellation. Even with that held back, it feels like "Ebenezer" is more a proving ground than impassioned adaptation, with West demonstrating he can do more than just indie horror, and Depp showing more of his restraint as a performer. After all, this story is famously one about a loathsome man who learns contrition and seeks to make amends, and while the film itself never breaks the fourth wall with this idea, it comes damn close. What will happen to Depp the person is not for me to say, but he's going to have to work harder and take more risks than "Ebenezer" if he wants to give his screen career a second chance.

"Ebenezer" opens in theaters on November 13, 2026.

#145. Kate Middleton Opens Up About Her Cancer Recovery: “It Will Take Time”

📅 12 Nov 2026

Kate Middleton Opens Up About Her Cancer Recovery: “It Will Take Time”

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.vanityfair.com/story/kate-middleton-cancer-recovery

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, kate middleton has spoken about her cancer diagnosis and long treatment journey in a lengthy interview for country life magazine, conducted by writer robert macfarlane, an author known for his books on landscapes and the natural world. This special issue features Prince William as a guest editor, following in the footsteps of other members of the British royal family who previously served as guest editors for Country Life, including King Charles, Queen Camilla, and Princess Anne.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “i was told in hospital that my recovery would not be linear. There will be good days and bad days, that it will take time,” said the Princess of Wales. “It shows us that periods of rest, reflection, and renewal are equally as important as moments of growth,” said Kate. As such, her love of nature played a vital role during her treatment. This perspective offers a different view of recovery: not as a phase to be overcome as quickly as possible, but as a time when pausing, listening to oneself, and replenishing one’s energy becomes an integral part of the healing process.

Diungkapkan bahwa in the interview, she also spoke about the therapeutic value of the natural environment, to which she has always shown a particular affinity. “Whether it is the beach for healing and recovery, the countryside for peace and perspective, or the mountains to find solitude, people have long sought comfort in the natural world. It is such a restorative environment, and incorporating nature into someone’s recovery pathway is vital,” she said.

Sebagaimana diketahui, after experiencing illness firsthand, the princess was particularly interested in a holistic approach to treatment and healing. Yes, serious illness creates a lot of physical challenges, but there is also a deeper part to all of us. “What I feel really passionate about, having had firsthand experience, is approaching illness and recovery through a whole-person approach. Nature has allowed me to find a deeper connection to my mind, body, and spirit,” she said.

Diungkapkan bahwa kate then explained what she found in the natural environment and why she considers it so precious: “it doesn’t ask anything of us. It simply allows us to be. ” She continued, “It really has been my sanctuary and a place I’ve instinctively wanted to go. It doesn’t judge us or expect us to perform. ”.

The Princess of Wales playing with a little girl.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the princess of wales reflected on her childhood, recounting how she spent a great deal of time outdoors from a very young age. “I remember from a very early age spending a lot of time in nature, playing in streams, walking in the countryside, blackberry picking, or simply time alone in my own world, enjoying the simplicity of ordinary things. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, among the memories she shared is one that’s particularly evocative: when she used to dig under bushes, convinced she’d find treasure. “When we are little, we seem to notice things more. A simple game, born of a little girl’s imagination, that transformed a corner of the garden into a place full of possibilities. Sadly, this is something I think we lose touch with as adults. “There was always a sense of freedom I felt in nature, something about being outdoors that is hard to find elsewhere,” she explained. Like the changing light through the trees, the sound of water, the joy of crunching leaves or finding a feather. These moments can seem ordinary, but, often, they’re the things we remember most. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, according to the princess, as we grow up, we risk losing this ability to observe and appreciate the little details. Life becomes more hectic, commitments multiply, and we end up forgetting how important it is to stop, slow down, and pay attention to the little things.

The smiling princess at Chase Community Hospital in Bordon.

Diungkapkan bahwa at one point, macfarlane asked the princess of wales a particularly profound question: where does she find hope? the writer observed that, in his view, despair is almost a luxury we cannot afford. Kate responded by returning to the theme running through the conversation: the lessons of the natural world. “We might not be able to have certainty or control every outcome, but we can do the small things, and those small things add up and do make a difference, if we nurture what is around us and have faith. “I find hope in the lessons nature teaches us: that, despite the challenges life may throw at us, we are not alone, and that we are interconnected with something bigger than ourselves,” she said. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa kate went public with her cancer diagnosis in march 2024, after undergoing abdominal surgery in january of that same year. At that time, however, she had already made it clear that the end of treatment would not automatically mean a full recovery: “Although I have finished chemotherapy, my path to healing and full recovery is long and I must continue to take each day as it comes. I am, however, looking forward to being back at work and undertaking a few more public engagements in the coming months when I can. The news shocked the entire world. In September 2024, she announced that she had completed her course of chemotherapy. ”.

Kate at Chase Community Hospital in Bordon.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, kate also spoke in the interview about her approach to motherhood, emphasizing her desire to give her children—prince george, princess charlotte, and prince louis—the freedom to explore the world at their own pace and according to their own curiosity. “It is something I remind myself to do with my own children; to give them freedom to explore, rather than constantly telling them what to see or what to think,” she said.

Diungkapkan bahwa the princess then expressed a specific concern: the rising anxiety among those in younger generations, who spend an increasingly significant portion of their lives online and surrounded by technology. “What worries me is the growing anxiety among children and young people. It’s a generation that’s more online and connected to tech than ever before," she stated. Nature is a natural environment where those skills can be built. “In this increasingly digital world, I believe it is more important than ever that children grow up with a strong sense of belonging, connection, and emotional security. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa interaction with the environment, she explained, offers children opportunities to practice important skills through hands-on experiences. It is essential for our well-being. “Whether it’s collecting leaves, building something from sticks, climbing a tree, or simply observing the world around them, children are constantly learning and discovering, about themselves, other people, and the world around them. “Nature also encourages curiosity, imagination, and creativity,” she said. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, macfarlane then linked these observations to the princess’s work on early childhood. He noted that Kate has repeatedly emphasized the importance of the first five years of life and asked her how nature could contribute to laying the foundations for development. The princess emphasized how central relationships are during early childhood: “So much of early childhood is about building nurturing environments that allow strong relationships to grow. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the princess explained that a child gradually develops various relationships: with themselves, with their parents or caregivers, with other children, and with the world around them. “The natural world gives children an extraordinary environment in which to develop those relationships,” she said. In this regard, she recalled her visit to Reggio Emilia, Italy—an experience she described as particularly meaningful because it allowed her to rediscover many of the principles that guide the work of her Centre for Early Childhood.

Diungkapkan bahwa among these is the importance of relationships, the environment, experiences, and, above all, the ability to truly listen to children. “Nature wasn’t another lesson; it offered an integral space that encouraged questions, that stimulated imagination, curiosity, and collaboration,” she explained.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, on the very same day the interview was published, kate visited chase community hospital in bordon, hampshire, to learn firsthand about the expansion of a project supported by the royal foundation’s centre for early childhood. The initiative aims to help identify more infants who, along with their families, may need additional support during the first months and years of life. During the visit, the princess met with health care workers, professionals, and families involved in using the Alarm Distress Baby Scale, known by the acronym ADBB. This observation tool, which she learned about during her visit to Copenhagen, enables health care providers to identify early signs of social and relational withdrawal in children.

The princess with some health care workers.

#146. Why The Lord Of The Rings: The Rings Of Power Season 3 Feels Like A Reboot [Exclusive]

📅 12 Nov 2026

Why The Lord Of The Rings: The Rings Of Power Season 3 Feels Like A Reboot [Exclusive]

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2314477/why-the-lord-of-the-ring-the-rings-of-power-season-3-feels-like-reboot/

Berdasarkan laporan, keep it secret, keep it safe. from spoilers. This article discusses major plot details from Episodes 1-4 of "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" Season 3.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the world is changed," cate blanchett's galadriel intones in the very first words of "the lord of the rings: the fellowship of the ring. " In the Peter Jackson film, the Elven royal is mourning the passing of the ages. The Season 3 premiere quickly establishes that, following a five-year time jump, Middle-earth is not the same as before. In "The Rings of Power," viewers may feel a similar sense of time slipping by as they tune into the first four episodes released by Prime Video. War rages, certain characters now play very different roles, and things have never felt quite so dire.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the rings of power" may still struggle to live up to the hype, but there's no mistaking that sense of starting over this time around. After a relatively up-and-down journey to this point, was Season 3 meant to be a creative reset for newcomers to jump on board? That was one of my biggest burning questions when I sat down with series co-showrunner Patrick McKay during a recent press junket. While stopping just short of endorsing a complete 180-degree pivot in approach, he admitted this was very much intended to keep viewers on their toes:.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "the big thing is, honestly, we want to keep shaking things up. Seasons 1 and 2 kind of roll straight through, linearly. And this time, it felt like a good opportunity to shake things up and drop you in a story in a place you're not expecting. We want to surprise the audience. We want to come at you with a pitch you haven't seen yet. ".

Diungkapkan bahwa for those who've watched all four episodes released to this point, it's abundantly clear that "the rings of power" isn't messing around this season. Not only has Charlie Vickers' Sauron finally unmasked himself and declared open war upon all free peoples, but the writers themselves have developed a bit of a ruthless streak. Multiple characters are killed off in the early going, neither of whom had much of a place in the ongoing story anymore, while even the Hobbit-like clan of Harfoots from Seasons 1 and 2 are now completely missing in action.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, taken as a whole, it's a promising (if overdue) development for viewers who have struggled with the show's unwieldy ensemble cast and patience-testing armada of subplots. After a few table-setting sequences, Season 3 begins with a major battle sequence that confirms how overmatched our heroes really are. Sauron's power has grown, his fearsome proto-Ringwraiths (known as Nazgnagôl) are now in thrall, and, of course, the threat of the One Ring overshadows everything. For Patrick McKay, however, this all goes back to the desire to avoid lulling viewers into a predictable pattern of storytelling,  instead coming right out of the gate swinging. As McKay told me, this season was the perfect opportunity to take a really big swing:.

Berdasarkan laporan, "that was very much a conscious choice. We [previously] built to big events and big battles. And we love those seasons, I'm very proud of them. We wanted to invert the structure of the prior couple seasons. But we wanted to do something different and we felt like, 'What if we started with a battle? What if we started at the height of the war and then maybe hit the ground running?'.

Berdasarkan laporan, there's a lot to be said for spending years carefully establishing the tone and structure of a mega-budget streaming show. As "The Rings of Power" hits its middle act in Season 3 (remember, this was planned to last five full seasons), the timing couldn't be better to kick things into another gear. only to upend the board at its halfway point. As the villains of the story gain the upper hand and our heroes race to catch up, the creative team applied a similar mindset to the experience of actually watching this season unfold.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "look, as viewers, j. [Payne], my co-showrunner and I, we love chasing a show," Patrick McKay revealed to me. D. " That, as it turns out, helped influence their decision to pull a similar trick with "The Rings of Power. "When you're in a movie theater, and you can feel an audience keying in and chasing the film, it's always great, and it makes your investment even more powerful. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, "if you're entering a story at a point where it's in medias res and you've got to kind of figure it out and [you go], 'oh wow, galadriel and arondir [the elf character played by ismael cruz córdova] are friends now and, oh my gosh, barad-dûr has been built and oh, that must be rivendell and what is this?' it's kind of an exciting way to watch something. ".

Berdasarkan laporan, clearly, the hope is for this chapter of "the rings of power" to provide a jolt and give fans reason to stick around. After the four-episode premiere, we have half a season left to see where this goes. Two new episodes drop on Prime Video on November 18, 2026.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, elsewhere in the episode, jo (camilla luddington) delivered friend corrie’s (sarah levy) baby in the back of an ambulance after major complications. Instead of being triggered by the procedure, Jo realized she wanted to return to work.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, grey’s anatomy has had its fair share of shakeups this season with an even more limited number of episodes. The medical drama previously had as many as 27 episodes per season, but this year, there are only 13.

#153. The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping Will Be A Bigger Box Office Hit Than You Realize

📅 12 Nov 2026

The Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping Will Be A Bigger Box Office Hit Than You Realize

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2313974/the-hunger-games-sunrise-on-the-reaping-box-office-preview/

Sebagaimana diketahui, one of the biggest expected hits of the fall season is nearly upon us — and it's going to be even bigger than a lot of people realize. "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" will explore Haymitch Abernathy's origin story, with Woody Harrelson having popularized the character in the original run of "Hunger Games" films. This time, Joseph Zada is playing the younger Haymitch, and it turns out folks are very eager to see how he ended up winning his games in his youth.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, once again directed by franchise shepherd francis lawrence, "sunrise on the reaping" is currently eyeing a monster box office opening between $105 and $140 million domestically when it arrives next weekend, per box office theory. These estimates have climbed a lot in recent weeks, so I'm personally included to lean on the higher end of projections. Either way, it's going to be a dramatic improvement for the property.

Diungkapkan bahwa in 2023, "the hunger games: the ballad of songbirds and snakes" topped the box office, but lionsgate wasn't partying like it's 2012. 6 million en route to $349 million worldwide. All of "The Hunger Games" movies have been hits at the box office, yet that prequel's grosses were far behind the previous entries, which all opened north of $100 million and made at least $650 million worldwide. It opened to $44. This latest prequel is, by all appearances, going to be more in line with those earlier entries.

Berdasarkan laporan, "sunrise on the reaping" takes place more than two decades before the first-ever "hunger games" film/book and four decades after "the ballad of songbirds & snakes. " Its story is focused on the 50th annual Hunger Games, aka the Second Quarter Quell, in which Haymitch famously competed and won before mentoring Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) in the 74th Hunger Games.

Sebagaimana diketahui, why is the latest "hunger games" prequel expected to perform so much better than its predecessor? for one, author suzanne collins' source novel was incredibly well received, telling a story many have been curious about for a long time. For another, Jennifer Lawrence is reprising Katniss for "Sunrise on the Reaping," with Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson coming back as Peeta Mellark and the older Haymitch as well.

Diungkapkan bahwa while these appearances should be fairly brief, getting the band back together absolutely helps make this more of an event for fans. Similarly, "The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes" was about the insidious President Snow's origins, whereas casual audiences are probably more interested in learning about Haymich's backstory. Lionsgate spent over/under $200 million to make "Sunrise on the Reaping," which was risky in light of how "Songbirds and Snakes" performed, but it's currently shaping up to be money well spent.

Diungkapkan bahwa the last time the franchise saw a hit of this size was when 2015's "the hunger games: mockingjay — part 2" opened to $102 million domestically en route to $653 million in theaters worldwide. If this film opens on the higher end of projections? It could be closer to "Catching Fire" ($158 million opening/$865 million worldwide). Either way, this is going to be the biggest opening of the fall season to date, by far.

Diungkapkan bahwa early reactions to "sunrise on the reaping" have been largely positive, which also bodes well. And while Thanksgiving will bring in big competition like "Focker In-Law" and Disney's "Hexed," it falls over one of the biggest moviegoing weeks of the year. As such, all these films should be able to co-exist.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" hits theaters on November 20, 2026.

In many ways, streaming viewership remains a great mystery.

Berdasarkan laporan, the movie is based on the book of the same name by n. Richard Nash. It takes place in the late 1970s and focuses on a former rodeo star named Mike Milo (Eastwood) who takes a job from an ex‐boss to bring his young son home, taking him away from his alcoholic mom. Crossing rural Mexico on their back way to Texas, the unlikely pair faces an unexpectedly challenging journey.

Berdasarkan laporan, eastwood's "cry macho" flopped in theaters five years ago, but there are many reasons for that. decided to premiere its entire 2021 movie slate on HBO Max and in theaters on the same day. That killed a lot of people's motivation to leave the house, which was already low.

Diungkapkan bahwa be that as it may, more than five years later, people appear to be catching up with this one now that it's on a new platform and available to watch from the comfort of home. The film's current popularity speaks volumes about Clint Eastwood's continued draw as an American cinema icon, both as an actor and a director. Westerns, in particular, have been the bread and butter for him dating back to his early days as an actor.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the legendary filmmaker has starred in many classics of the genre, including "the good, the bad, and the ugly" and "unforgiven," arguably the best movie directed by eastwood. So even if "Cry Macho" wasn't considered to be among his best works as a director, it still scratches an itch for viewers — especially viewers who have a certain nostalgia for Eastwood wearing a cowboy hat and boots.

Berdasarkan laporan, /film called "cry macho" an "old-fashioned cowboy drama" in our review from 2021. What makes the movie significant, above all else, is that it's probably going to serve as Eastwood's swan song within the genre and could quite possibly mark his final on-screen performance. It was a mixed review overall, which is pretty much how most critics felt about it. He's well into his 90s and there is a decent chance he's effectively retired at this point.

Berdasarkan laporan, 2024's intense courtroom drama "juror #2" was expected to be eastwood's final go-around as a director, which notably didn't feature him as an actor. Bearing that in mind, it's probably worth watching "Cry Macho" for a great many folks, if only as a send-off of sorts to one of the greatest to ever do it in the genre he's mostly closely associated with.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the premiere of hulu's 12 dates of christmas on the 2026 tv schedule serves as a mini reunion for pretty little liars fans, as it reunites hale and harding for the holiday flick. Hale plays Christina, a workaholic who owns a furniture restoration shop and has made little time for finding her romantic soulmate. After a disastrous family Christmas Eve dinner, Christina makes a promise to herself and her mom that by next year she’ll have someone to bring to it. Of course, the year gets away from her, which leads her best friend (Kahyun Kim) to set up a string of dates for Christina to go on in the twelve weeks leading up to Christmas Eve.

Netflix’s A Dog’s Perfect Christmas Made Me Cry, But Not For The Reasons I Thought.

Diungkapkan bahwa not to mention, this is a christmas romance movie, which means the town christina grew up in and still calls home isn’t a big one. All the more reason for her family to at least recognize Peter’s name, especially since he’s renovating his family’s home.

Berdasarkan laporan, ultimately, christina’s family not knowing who peter is isn’t that big of a deal. However, I do think it would have been a fun twist if they did recognize him because it would make them meddle in her love life even more. Still, 12 Dates of Christmas is a cute and festive Christmas flick that anyone with a Hulu subscription should definitely check out.

Berdasarkan laporan, garfield, who rose to prominence in projects like "doctor who" and "lions for lambs" before earning international fame and acclaim for his pivotal role in "the social network," is genuinely one of the most talented performers of his generation. You could point to any number of his projects and make a case, but I'm going to say that Garfield should have an Oscar for playing "Rent" writer Jonathan Larson in the 2021 movie musical "Tick. Tick. Boom!" (for which he did earn a Best Actor nomination).

Diungkapkan bahwa even if you're not a reformed musical theater kid like me, you know about "rent" — but generally, we need to talk about "tick. Before "Rent," Larson — who died at the age of 35 in 1996 after suffering from an aortic dissection — penned the mostly-autobiographical "Tick. Tick. Tick. Boom!" about his struggles to make it in musical theater, coming on the heels of his failed futuristic musical "Superbia. " Initially written as a solo show performed just by Larson on piano, the musical got a full-length treatment thanks to David Auburn after Larson's tragic passing, and "Hamilton" and "In the Heights" scribe Lin-Manuel Miranda adapted it into a film that released on November 12, 2021. Boom!" way more. Garfield's performance as Larson is electrifying, pitch-perfect, and gripping, and he should have an Oscar for it.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the "plot" of "tick. Tick. Boom!" is relatively simple — Andrew Garfield plays Jonathan Larson as he works days at the Moondance Diner and spends his free time perfecting that aforementioned musical "Superbia" for an upcoming workshop. Along the way, he grapples with the idea of leaving the arts behind for a more lucrative and stable career — like his best friend Michael (Robin de Jesús), who works for an ad agency — while also stressing about turning 30 years old.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, if you're familiar with "rent," you may not be surprised to learn that the hiv-aids crisis plays a role; his friend freddy (ben levi ross) is hiv-positive, and it's eventually revealed that michael is as well. As Jonathan tries to manage his personal and professional lives, he crosses paths with his idol Stephen Sondheim (played by Bradley Whitford, though the real Sondheim did lend his voice to an answering machine message before he passed away in 2021) and frets about whether or not "Superbia" has any chance of success.

Berdasarkan laporan, usually, the gift of hindsight doesn't really serve an actor, but i think knowing that larson passed away before "rent" won a pulitzer prize (and tonys) gives garfield a great perspective here. His Jonathan is frenetic, a live wire, and lives his life to the fullest; Garfield's passionate performance throughout the film paints a picture of a man who's running out of time, and even though that's obviously expressed through the character's anxieties about turning 30, it's also a poignant representation of an artist whose life was cut tragically short. and in numbers like "Why," "30/90," and "Louder than Words," Garfield pays perfect homage to Larson's life and legacy.

Diungkapkan bahwa i think i've been pretty clear about the fact that andrew garfield should have an oscar for "tick. Tick. Boom!" He should, however, have won his second Oscar for that movie — because Garfield should have an Academy Award for best supporting actor for playing Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin in "The Social Network. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, under careful direction from david fincher and working with one of aaron sorkin's all-time best scripts — which he ultimately betrayed with his dog-brained sequel "the social reckoning" — garfield is extraordinary as eduardo, best friend to jesse eisenberg's mark zuckerberg who provides money and support during the initial founding of facebook. In one timeline, we see Mark and Eduardo as Harvard University students trying to get their social media platform off the ground; in another, we see Eduardo suing Mark after Mark cruelly cuts Eduardo out of the company and brings his shares down drastically on the advice of new partner Sean Parker (a ridiculously well-cast Justin Timberlake).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, garfield should probably have several awards just for the way he delivers the line "sorry, my prada's at the cleaners, along with my hoodie and my f***-you flip flops" to eisenberg's mark after he discovers his betrayal. Garfield needs to be taken more seriously as an actor across the board, and an Oscar nomination for "Tick. Boom!" is a good start. In my opinion, though? He should be swimming in a pool full of trophies every day when he wakes up. Tick. Tick. and he should have Oscars for "The Social Network" and "Tick. but throughout the entire film, he's uniformly excellent as a man whose closest friend is also the most destructive force in his life. Boom!" Because the musical is a Netflix original, you can screen it there and see for yourself.

Here are six of the best-looking special editions.

Diungkapkan bahwa sometimes, it feels like japan gets all the cool stuff. The JoyCons were a lovely blue. All in all, despite the apparent lack of ambition, it’s like a warm mug of cocoa on a chilly day.

The system’s base itself is white with gray print, featuring an intricate design that is enhanced by a splotch of bright yellow “paint” on its left portion. Berdasarkan laporan, the best zelda games are mythical, with strange symbols and patterns scattered around hyrule, and that design translated beautifully to the system capturing the feel of the legend of zelda: tears of the kingdom. Berdasarkan laporan, the animal crossing: new horizons console proved difficult to acquire during the initial weeks following its release, largely because no one could have anticipated just what a monster success that game would become. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, the special edition switch 2 console for the legend of zelda: ocarina of time is the first of its kind for nintendo’s latest hardware, which makes it the best-looking by default. Hopefully, Nintendo will produce more units to meet the demand, especially now that the game has shifted more than 5 million units in less than a month. Its two JoyCons are a deep metallic green, with Triforce shapes printed in still darker tones, along with a golden print on the left one. An ornate Triforce pattern appears at the very center, with faded echoes extending left. The console’s base is half black and half gold, with triangle-shaped print along its right side. That’s a distinction it is likely to retain, thanks to a stylish design. People are clearly all about Zelda this year, and the special edition console is the perfect way to celebrate that moment.

#174. Victorian Psycho Review: Maika Monroe Goes Crazy In This Erratic Mix Of Humor And Horror

📅 12 Nov 2026

Victorian Psycho Review: Maika Monroe Goes Crazy In This Erratic Mix Of Humor And Horror

Tanggal: 12 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2313694/victorian-psycho-review-maika-monroe-horror-movie/

Diungkapkan bahwa horror-comedies tend to lean heavier on the "comedy" side of things than the "horror. It makes for an erratic viewing experience — you begin to feel the film would be better served staying in one lane rather than trying to make concepts like dead babies funny. " But Zachary Wigon's "Victorian Psycho" attempts to do the opposite, giving the audience a gaggle of gruesome, unsettling moments punctuated by wry humor. Regardless, "Victorian Psycho" mostly succeeds due to Maika Monroe, who gives everything she's got as Winifred Notty, a psychotic governess who moves in with a wealthy family and proceeds to pile up a body count.

Sebagaimana diketahui, her attempt at an english accent may be a bit spotty, but monroe's commitment to playing crazy ultimately works, and works well. not well. If the film's title (an obvious nod to "American Psycho") wasn't a dead giveaway, it's clear from the jump that Winifred is. Her wry narration guides us through outlandish, blood-drenched moments as she spins a twisted tale. A suspicious past follows her as she arrives at Ensor House, inhabited by the Pounds family.

Diungkapkan bahwa winifred may be deranged, but the poundses aren't exactly a pleasant bunch. Mr. Pounds (Ruth Wilson) is cruel and ruthless with the staff, and the children Andrew (Jacobi Jupe) and Drusilla (Evie Templeton) have their own issues (Andrew is a brat destined to grow up to be a bully and Drusilla is more than a little creepy). Pounds (Jason Isaacs) is oblivious, Mrs. A sane person would take one look at the Pounds family and head for the hills, but of course, Winifred isn't sane.

Diungkapkan bahwa there's plenty of room for fun here, but "victorian psycho" is never confident enough in what it's trying to do. The performances are all very broad and big, save for the always-welcomed Thomasin McKenzie, playing the good-natured but clueless nurse Ms. Lamb, who becomes Winifred's only real friend (and instantly buys into her quickly concocted story about a ghoul roaming the grounds of Ensor House).

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as big and over-the-top as many of the elements here are, "victorian psycho" also seems to be trying to make a point about the subjugation of women in polite society. Yet it has no real insight into this beyond a surface level approach, and it's hard to get caught up in any sort of message when the film is also constantly pointing out how ridiculous everything here is.

Diungkapkan bahwa wigon, who previously directed "sanctuary," piles on some energetic camerawork that frequently mirrors winifred's fractured mind, but the script by virginia feito, adapting her own novel, relies too much on incessant narration that's not nearly as funny as it should be. And yet, "Victorian Psycho" remains perpetually watchable primarily due to Monroe's performance. A certified scream queen at this point in her career, it's a lot of fun to see Monroe cut loose and swing an axe at people's heads.

Sebagaimana diketahui, "victorian psycho" is just a little too unstable for its own good. There's a specific reason why Winifred has shown up at Ensor House, but the slow reveal of what's going on here feels undercooked. And when the film reaches its grand guignol finale, Wigon inexplicably starts pulling punches, robbing "Victorian Psycho" of a more satisfying conclusion and instead attempting something far more serious and dramatic than everything we've seen so far.

Berdasarkan laporan, what this all comes down to is me wanting to like "victorian psycho" a lot more than i ultimately did. I enjoyed Monroe's performance, and the film's morbidly funny atmosphere, but I came away from it all a tad unsatisfied. There's a ghoulish charm to the narrative, but the blood and guts of something far better is lurking somewhere in here, just out of sight.

"Victorian Psycho" opens in theaters on November 13, 2026.

Alex Consani at the 2026 LACMA Art + Film gala.

Berdasarkan laporan, i’m putting work into being a better actress. It’s a really exciting endeavor for me, especially considering all the projects that I’ve done that are coming out. Alex Consani with Sarah Paulson (left) and Leslie Grossman (right) in the sixth episode of American Horror Story: 13.

You and I are from the generations that grew up on Ryan Murphy shows.

Diungkapkan bahwa coven, for me, is my favorite american horror story season by far. What was it like to join the project? Did you audition? Did you get a call?.

Diungkapkan bahwa what i find so exciting about it is that it doesn’t feel as exclusive as fashion does, in a way. I’m very “divine timing” when it comes to this stuff, so I believe everything will happen and run its course in the way it should. But there’s also a lot of really interesting biopics that I would love to see. Maybe I write them, maybe I act. Who knows?.

Consani arriving at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art.

She’s so incredible with the way that she thinks. Wes Anderson is a really big one. I love Wes Anderson. There’s a lot of directors that I’m a big fan of, people who are obviously focused on cinematography, but also understand how to have fun.
