#182. 5 Sci-Fi Book Trilogies Where Every Entry Is Perfect

📅 13 Nov 2026

5 Sci-Fi Book Trilogies Where Every Entry Is Perfect

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/sci-fi-trilogy-perfect-entries/

The best sci-fi stories come in groups of three.

Sebagaimana diketahui, trilogies are a popular book format for a reason. Trilogies allow writers to flesh out their worlds, creating enough breathing room for genre concepts and important events. Apart from naturally satisfying the rule of three, they also naturally mimic the classic structure of a beginning, middle, and end. The same logic is particularly true for science fiction. Dystopian sci-fi books like The Hunger Games use the trilogy structure to map out the painstaking moving parts of a rebellion, while the Broken Earth science-fantasy trilogy encompasses a massive supercontinent full of complex lore.

Berdasarkan laporan, of course, not all sci-fi trilogies are created equal. But there are plenty of perfect trilogies, too. Polygon has rounded up five sci-fi book trilogies that are worth your time from start to finish. Plenty start strong only to flame out in book two or three, while others admittedly take a while to get good. Check out the list below.

Diungkapkan bahwa william gibson’s neuromancer is often at the forefront of brilliant cyberpunk book lists, given how foundational the text is for the genre. The first novel drops the reader in the midst of a bustling, neon-tinted city, where a console cowboy (hacker) named Case is forced into pulling off a heist in exchange for his continued survival. Its sequels, Count Zero and Mona Lisa Overdrive, tend to get overlooked in the process, even though these entries are as exceptional as Neuromancer. A sentient AI named Wintermute emerges as an antagonist, with Count Zero detailing the aftermath of the heist, and Mona Lisa Overdrive exposing the rotten core of a hyper-technological world.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, sprawl is the definition of “show, don’t tell. Sprawl is also a bleak, uncompromising look at corporate oppression, a sentiment that has inspired the core conflict in everything from The Matrix to Cyberpunk 2077. On the contrary, it invites the reader to decipher context cues and retains interest with strong character portraits. This doesn’t mean Sprawl isn’t immersive. ” This is a double-edged sword, as Gibson’s vivid prose can often feel more sensory than descriptive, making it unsuited for brisk reading. This aspect is substantial enough, but Sprawl drives it home with a reflective ending that makes human presence irrelevant to the progress of machine intelligence.

Diungkapkan bahwa although isaac asimov added two sequels and two prequels to the foundation novel series after 1953, the core concept was conceived as a trilogy. Seldon foresees the fall of the Empire, a lengthy dark age, and the eventual rise of a second empire. These novels — Foundation, Foundation and Empire, and Second Foundation — are set in the final days of a Galactic Empire, where mathematician Hari Seldon uses a special technique called psychohistory to predict the future. He decides to shorten the projected number of years between the rise and fall of a dynasty.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, asimov’s narrative scope in the foundation novels is massive. For Seldon, history becomes a malleable timeline instead of a fixed inevitability, which has its repercussions on the galaxy at large. The novels follow the fall of a 12,000-year-old Galactic Empire, which has been shaped by sociopolitical factors that cannot be erased by history on a whim. Seldon’s plan to shorten the duration of the dark age is grand and unprecedented, but it is one that causes repeated issues over time. The math, although solid, contains variables that were previously unaccounted for, turning the Foundation trilogy into a tense psychological mystery that plays by the rules of sci-fi.

Diungkapkan bahwa liu cixin creates a dense, compelling case for the limits of human nature and how these limits can be overcome through cold logic. Cixin’s Three-Body Problem offers a solid base for this idea, which turns into a full-blown conversation about civilizational entropy and cosmic forces in The Dark Forest and Death’s End. These complicated events begin with a disillusioned young woman named Ye Wenjie, who dooms humanity by inviting an alien race known as the Trisolarans to invade the planet. As the Trisolarans experience a vicious cycle of destruction and rebirth due to the three suns that orbit their system, Earth becomes both a source of salvation and a target for colonization.

Berdasarkan laporan, remembrance of earth’s past is full of promising characters like wang miao and luo ji, but cixin is more interested in representing humanity as a collective species. This leaves us vulnerable to threats of a cosmic scale. Not only are we horribly underprepared to deal with such a crisis, but we are also destined to perish according to the laws of science. Although internal differences remain, humanity is fundamentally driven by a need to survive, but this impulse is short-term. This fragility is at the core of Remembrance of Earth’s Past, which argues that the only way to adapt is to keep transcending at the cost of leaving our “human” identities behind.

Berdasarkan laporan, formerly known as the xenogenesis trilogy, octavia e. Butler’s Lilith’s Brood comprises Dawn, Adulthood Rites, and Imago. The story opens with a woman named Lilith being unable to recall her past, although she vaguely remembers a planet-wide catastrophic event and an accident that killed her family. Over time, Lilith realizes that an alien race known as the Oankali rescued a few survivors from an irradiated Earth, leaving humanity no choice but to evolve into a completely different species.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, lilith’s brood is a radical inversion of traditional “first contact” sci-fi tales. Instead, they propose a genetic trade, giving humans the choice to “upgrade” themselves, although this freedom to choose feels like an illusion. Earth is already uninhabitable, so the Oankali aren’t interested in inheriting a new planet or ruling over its people. The Oankali perceive humanity as paranoid, self-destructive beings who are also capable of high intelligence and deep empathy. This contradiction is at the heart of the series, as we’re left to wonder whether a forced evolution makes humanity lose these traits to the point that they become unrecognizable in their own eyes.

Sebagaimana diketahui, a sprawling look at the settlement and terraforming of mars, kim stanley robinson’s mars trilogy offers hard sci-fi realism. The science is mostly authentic, as Robinson is more preoccupied with the nuanced developments made on Mars while the condition on Earth deteriorates due to overpopulation and environmental disasters. The books (Red Mars, Blue Mars, and Green Mars) follow a group of colonists who are part of a joint American-Russian undertaking, and how they manage to build their first settlement on Mars and its hollowed-out moon.

Diungkapkan bahwa the mars trilogy is a multi-generational look at the rise of a new society. Rebuilding society from scratch is no walk in the park; the planet’s terrain proves to be a challenge, along with continental ice-melt floods. There’s also the human aspect of it all, as such a high-stakes project comes with conflict. Even in the absence of conflict, humans are entangled in their own unique problems, which the books unravel with the same interest as they do the scientific aspects of the resettlement. A rapidly declining Earth also becomes the point of focus, as the comparatively utopian life on Mars reminds humans how they ruined a perfectly hospitable planet tailor-made for their survival.

In addition, large chunks of Foundation were simply ripped off from the history of 6th century Byzantium.

#191. Tim Burton's Forgotten Dark Fantasy Magnum Opus Is Officially Free on Youtube

📅 13 Nov 2026

Tim Burton's Forgotten Dark Fantasy Magnum Opus Is Officially Free on Youtube

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/corpse-bride-streaming-free-youtube-november-2026/

And it pairs perfectly with another stop-motion movie currently in theaters.

Diungkapkan bahwa when it comes to beautiful, high-quality stop-motion animation, laika is likely the first name that comes to mind. Each has leaned toward more adult themes with gothic narrative undertones, while still focusing heavily on family dynamics. The studio’s hand-crafted puppetry and 3D-printing technology have brought beautiful tales to life for years, from Coraline to Kubo and the Two Strings. The same is true of Laika’s most recent outing, Travis Knight’s ethereal fantasy epic, Wildwood.

Berdasarkan laporan, yet as much a technical and emotional achievement as wildwood has proven to be, you don’t need to head to your local theater to see laika's best animated film. All you need to do is go to YouTube, where Tim Burton’s masterful 2005 Corpse Bride is streaming right now, for free.

Berdasarkan laporan, directed by tim burton and mike johnson, corpse bride follows victor van dort (johnny depp) and his arranged marriage to victoria everglot (emily watson). Without thinking, he says them aloud and slips his ring onto what he believes is a tree branch sticking out from the ground. After a terrible rehearsal dinner, Victor heads to the woods to practice his vows. But the “branch” is actually the finger of an undead bride, Emily (Helena Bonham Carter), who immediately assumes they’re engaged. Victor is soon dragged into the land of the dead, where he comes face-to-face with its inhabitants.

Sebagaimana diketahui, if the story sounds familiar, there’s a reason. However, instead of helping the undead bride find peace, the groom takes his dead spouse to a local rabbi, who annuls the marriage because his wife is dead. The bride falls to pieces into a pile of bones, and the groom goes on to live his life as if nothing ever happened. Burton was open about the fact that Corpse Bride was based on “The Finger”, a Jewish tale by author Howard Schwartz, and featured in “Lilith’s Cave: Jewish Tales of the Supernatural. ” In this tale, set in Russia rather than Victorian England, the young bridegroom also makes the same mistake as Victor, slipping his wedding ring onto a corpse's finger as he recites his vows. C’est la vie.

Berdasarkan laporan, that transition from a jewish folktale to a mainstream gothic fairy tale brought many changes. That meant Emily, the undead bride, found a more peaceful, fulfilling end, while Victor became more empathetic. As macabre and unsettling as Burton’s productions can be, he is undoubtedly a creator whose endings usually have a sweet quality — bitter or otherwise. It made sense: no matter how terrifying some of Burton’s films might seem, they usually target a family-friendly, universal audience.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “we wanted to make a version that wasn’t so disturbing that you couldn’t put it in a family movie,” corpse bride’s co-screenwriter john august explained in an interview with jewish journal. As for the setting and the change to non-Jewish characters, August said Burton gravitates toward “universal, fairy-tale qualities in his films. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, much about corpse bride was a first for many of the film's cast and crew. Burton, for example, had produced many stop-motion animated films before, such as The Nightmare Before Christmas (1993) and James and the Giant Peach (1996). Corpse Bride was Burton's first stop-motion directing credit, though he mostly took a backseat as co-director due to simultaneously working on Charlie and the Chocolate Factory. This left Johnson to take what he describes as a more “organic” approach to directing.

Diungkapkan bahwa “tim knew where he wanted the film to go as far as the emotional tone and story points to hit,” johnson explained in an interview with creative planet network. “My job was to work with the crew on a daily basis and get the footage as close as possible to how I thought he wanted it. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, burton still had exclusive control over storyboards, concepts, and scenes, and each one had to be reviewed and approved before johnson could say it was finished. But for the meat of production, Johnson was in charge.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, johnson being in charge, however, didn’t mean that corpse bride lost burton’s distinct style. Burton has never shied away from his macabre, stark aesthetic. Even his less well-received works, such as his Alice in Wonderland adaptations, feature a clear visual divide that makes the contrast appealing while still conveying his distinctly Burton-esque style. The Red Queen’s castle, for example, looks and feels very different from the Mad Hatter’s tea party.

Diungkapkan bahwa burton’s use of contrast makes corpse bride an enigma at first. Everything seems the same: the world of the living is steeped in dreary gray and black, making every character appear miserable and depleted by the world they inhabit. Ironically, true life begins only when we reach the land of the dead: an explosion of yellow, green, blue, and red. The dead have more life and music, truly living as they wish, with the freedom death has granted them.

Sebagaimana diketahui, as for laika, the stop-motion studio co-produced corpse bride as its first official project after current ceo and wildwood director travis knight took over what had been will vinton studios. Four years later, it released its debut feature, the very Burton-esque Coraline, directed by Henry Selick, before charting its own course as a leading stop-motion studio. Years later, every Laika project still carries a hint of Burton's childlike wonder and gothic beauty.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, flipping audiences’ expectations of what they'll see has always been a signature trait of both burton and laika. As one of the highest-grossing animated films of all time, Corpse Bride’s success makes it easy to see why it remains so beloved more than 20 years later.

Corpse Bride is available to stream on HBO Max now.

#195. Netflix’s ‘The Body’ Explores Queer Girlhood, Catholic Guilt, and the Teenage Search for Faith

Netflix’s ‘The Body’ Explores Queer Girlhood, Catholic Guilt, and the Teenage Search for Faith

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.vanityfair.com/story/netflix-the-body-geena-meszaros

“Confess!” yells a teen as she stares into a pack of wide-eyed Catholic schoolgirls.

Berdasarkan laporan, “i made out with katie’s dad,” one reveals. “I masturbate to Daddy Franklin!” another cries, a black cross still smudged on her forehead.

Diungkapkan bahwa welcome to the body, a new netflix series that recalls a holy trinity of inspirations: carrie, jennifer’s body, and heavenly creatures. But while all three were reference points for the show’s star, Geena Meszaros, she also wants her character to stand alone. “I really wanted her to be her own thing,” she told VF in October.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “it was kismet,” meszaros says of landing the role of lisbeth. “I feel like she was my dream character to play before I even realized it. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the body is set in a catholic girls school circa the early 2000s—complete with juicy couture pajamas, yahoo! messenger, teenage devilry, secret lesbian relationships, and plenty of catholic guilt. Meszaros plays Lisbeth, a gawky reject whose desperation to join the dance team leads her to some fairly sinful decisions. On Halloween night, mutually pining co-captains Anya (Kristina Bogic) and Elise (Sara Boustany) stage a team initiation that goes wildly wrong—and maybe accidentally summons the devil.

Sebagaimana diketahui, amid the chaos of their drunken houseparty, lisbeth takes one for the team and buries a body—literally. Before long, high school devolves into Crucible-style mania as the girls start seeing visions.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, though showrunner quinn shephard has described the body as a love letter to the female-centered horror of the early 2000s, and it arrives amid a similarly themed carrie remake and the nov. 20 return of Yellowjackets; the series might be less of a Y2K echo than something entirely new: a snapshot of Gen Z’s faith in 2026.

“There's a sense of faith in each other, that you need to have, that you just don't get if you're not part of a team,” Meszaros says about connecting with her costars.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, meszaros calls the show a mix of horror, comedy, and grittiness, all smushed together. There’s also a bit of romance overseen by Chala Hunter, the same intimacy coordinator who worked on Heated Rivalry. (“I don’t know if I’ve met anyone who’s just so themselves all the time,” Meszaros says of her costar. Meanwhile, a very pregnant Gabby Windey makes her acting debut as the team’s coach. ).

Like Meszaros, almost everyone else in the cast is an up-and-comer: Kristina Bogic, who plays the popular high school sweetheart Anya; Sara Boustany, who plays her wicked best friend (and secret lover) Elise; Sofia Wylie, the doomed preacher’s niece; and Nnamdi Asomugha, an NFL cornerback turned actor who plays that very preacher (and the school’s principal): Father (Daddy) Franklin.

“I'm more of a spiritual person, but I think having faith in anything outside of yourself, whether that's God or whether that's something else, I think that's important,” Meszaros says.

#200. The Best Ways For Star Trek Fans To Play Magic's New Set: A Guide For Beginner Players

📅 11 Nov 2026

The Best Ways For Star Trek Fans To Play Magic's New Set: A Guide For Beginner Players

Tanggal: 11 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.slashfilm.com/2314044/star-trek-magic-the-gathering-new-set-beginners-guide/

Diungkapkan bahwa when i sat down at my friendly local game store to participate in a pre-release drafting event for magic: the gathering's new "star trek" set, several players saw the enterprise tattoo on my forearm and asked me the same question. If a longtime Magic player wanted to sample "Star Trek," what was the best place for them to start?.

Ironically, I was there to ask the Mirror Universe version of that same question: If a longtime "Star Trek" fan wanted to sample the new Magic set, what's the best place for them to start?.

Diungkapkan bahwa i am new to magic, having only picked up the game a few months ago to prime myself for the new "trek" release. And one thing Magic and "Star Trek" have in common is that they're both absolutely daunting at first blush. One is a collectible card game with over 30 years of history and dozens of ways to play. The other is a sci-fi universe with nearly 1,000 episodes of television and 13 movies, with dozens of possible entry points.

Sebagaimana diketahui, i can answer one question immediately. (This is a sometimes controversial opinion, but I stick by it. "Trek" newbies should start with "Star Trek: Strange New Worlds," with its glossy production values and modern streaming sensibilities, before backtracking and sampling the various other shows and finding the one that connects with their tastes. ).

Sebagaimana diketahui, but the other question involved some legwork, a lot of time spent at a gaming table, a great deal more time sorting through cards, and even a question proposed to the lead designers of the set itself. So, what is the best way for a "Star Trek" fan to sample the new Magic: The Gathering set? Here's what I learned.

Berdasarkan laporan, one thing i will not do here is explain the rules of magic: the gathering, which are intuitive and easy to learn, but challenging to master. There are countless online resources to learn before you try anything I recommend below. I'm writing this piece under the assumption you intend to seek those out on your own.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the best way to truly dive in headfirst is to visit your local gaming shop and participate in a sealed or drafting event. Naturally, this is dependent on your location and whether your local gaming shop is an inviting and safe space (shout out to Mothership Games in Austin, Texas for playing host to my first sealed event). If such a place exists for you, check the calendar and see what's on offer. The good news is that the "Star Trek" set is brand new and there should be plenty of opportunities.

Sebagaimana diketahui, at events like these, players are organized into one-on-one matches and construct their decks from scratch, tearing open booster packs, examine their cards, and trying to build the most effective strategy possible around a 40-card deck. And "Star Trek" fans should take very easily to this format, since the characters you'd expect to be powerful tend to have cards that are powerful. While experienced players will have an edge, they can't bring finely honed and powerful decks from home to immediately wipe the floor with you. Everyone starts at square one. It also leads to some amusing team-ups, like how my winning deck involved an unlikely alliance between Deanna Troi and Gul Dukat.

Diungkapkan bahwa in a friendly shop with a friendly crowd, this is magic at its purest: a direct, competitive game where tactics at the table are as important as the strategy behind your deck construction. And the mechanics in the "Trek" set are intuitive and mesh well, meaning that creating a deck that functions as needed is fairly straightforward, and going with your gut choices (i. e. , building around characters you like) often leads to strong results.

I can hear your next question: You don't have access to a local shop, or you don't feel comfortable going to one, so what's the best way to play at home? Once again, there are options.

Diungkapkan bahwa you and a friend (or more) could always buy booster packs, tearing them open and building personal collections and constructing 60-card decks for standard play. However, I would recommend booster packs being the start of your collection, and once you have bought a few, track down single cards to complete your strategy rather than buying more and blindly hoping for strong pulls.

Sebagaimana diketahui, another option is for you and a friend to buy a pre-release kit, as there are always plenty leftover after the initial week of special event. Use these to construct imperfect but fun starter decks to learn the game, and then grow and expand those decks as you see fit, doubling down on the characters and strategies you're enjoying.

However, the best at-home experience would be to pick up one of the set's Draft Night boxes, which are pricy but offer bang for your buck: enough cards for four friends to craft decks and go head-to-head for an evening, leaving everyone with enough cards to build upon in the future.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, however, all of these options require tinkering, and suggest that you'll enjoy the process of building a deck as much as playing one. These options require additional legwork, additional financial investment, and even a bit of luck (although that can be mitigated by buying single cards from reputable online and brick-and-mortar shops). If you want to truly just dive into the game itself and skip the rest of the process, there is another way.

When I had a chance to speak to the key designers behind Magic: The Gathering's "Star Trek" set during a launch event in Los Angeles, I asked if the new set was friendly for "Star Trek" fans with no gaming experience, and if they had a recommendation on where to start.

Diungkapkan bahwa first, they noted that the set was designed with new players in mind and puts narrative first. A card will generally behave like its counterpart in the "Star Trek" universe, so a fan knows that a Captain Kirk card will be a bit more headstrong and aggressive while Spock will allow for more wily, thoughtful strategy. This means a "Trek" fan should be able to grasp the new cards fairly quickly, using their existing knowledge as a crutch.

Second, they highlighted their recommendation for the best way to sample the game: the "Star Trek" commander decks.

Berdasarkan laporan, commander is the most popular format in magic, where players utilize 100 card decks in four-player games that are slowly paced, socially driven, and generally take an entire evening to play. Many Magic sets are accompanied by a few pre-constructed commander decks, which players can purchase, open, and play immediately without any prep. Think of them as more of a board game experience — or a nerd poker night — than a standard Magic set. The "Star Trek" set has four of them: Federation Fleet, We Are the Borg, Klingon Fury, and Landing Party.

Specifically, the designers recommended the Federation Fleet commander deck as their choice for a "Star Trek" fan hoping to play the game.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, naturally, the next step was to test the designers' suggestion. I rounded up three friends and assigned them each a different Star Trek commander deck, taking Federation Fleet for myself. It's easy to see why this one was recommended: With Picard on the cover and a deck full of '90s "Trek" staples, it's the most popular era of the franchise in one 100-card deck.

Sebagaimana diketahui, our four-player game took over three hours, and frankly, it was some of the best magic i've ever played, with all four decks interacting in surprising and wild ways that left everyone at the table screaming and laughing. My victory told a story in of itself: Dr. The "Trek" fans were impressed by the thematic touches, and how the mechanics relate to character personalities and motives, while the Magic players simply relished in the new design elements. I squeaked out a win, but only after the Borg player staged a comeback that essentially wiped out the table. Bashir threw himself at the Borg player, perishing, but in the process, activated his ability to resurrect Ro Laren from the dead, activating her ability and ending the Borg threat once and for all.

Diungkapkan bahwa after seeing the commander decks in action, i'm inclined to agree with the designers' recommendation. The Landing Part deck, with its focus on Original Series characters, is fairly straightforward, but has a lot of moving pieces to consider. The Borg deck is scary and powerful, but makes them an immediate threat the other players will team up against to defeat. The Klingon deck is pure aggression, which may work against a new player's inherent shyness. The mechanical simplicity of the Federation Fleet deck, and its arsenal of beloved characters, makes it easy to grasp and understand quickly.

Sebagaimana diketahui, much like with "star trek" itself, there are countless ways to get into magic: the gathering, and no incorrect way. Ultimately, I agree with the designers: the pre-constructed commander decks, and specifically the Federation Fleet deck, are the best point of entry. Ideally, you'd buy all four and learn with friends for the best possible experience.

But like with "Star Trek" itself, you should be warned: once Magic has sucked you in, be prepared to be sucked in for the long haul.

#203. Netflix's Disappointing New Western Thriller Wastes Its Brilliant Concept

Netflix's Disappointing New Western Thriller Wastes Its Brilliant Concept

Tanggal: 13 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.polygon.com/heartland-netflix-review/

Chastain stars in Netflix's new musical western.

Diungkapkan bahwa jessica chastain’s career has taken many turns. More recently, she was nominated for a Tony and helmed the buzzy horror movie Other Mommy, which made an impact at the box office but got trashed by critics. She was nominated for her acting work (Zero Dark Thirty, The Eyes of Tammy Faye) or as part of a larger ensemble (The Martian, Interstellar). For a time, she was one of the Academy’s most beloved actresses, appearing in films that made their way deep into the awards conversation. Her Apple TV thriller The Savant was postponed because of its subject matter, inspiring a wider conversation on politics. But for all those twists, turns, and bumps in the road, Heartland might be her most delirious project yet.

Berdasarkan laporan, written and directed by shana feste, the netflix-original film feels as if the director of country strong watched a couple of episodes of yellowstone and decided to take a stab at a western-noir, centering her story on a jaded country star. The result is a missing-person mystery with three musical numbers woven into it. Heartland might be the first western-noir-musical ever made, and I wish Feste took advantage of how weird that is. Instead, it’s pure straight-to-Netflix fodder.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, chastain stars as misty jones, a country singer living in seclusion. Misty threatens the neighbor and shoots out her windows. Then she gets drunk and has a one-night stand. The first time we see her, she's crying over her dog, who’s been shot and killed by the neighbor. Her successful past is alluded to when she opens her fridge to reveal moldy food sitting right next to a Grammy Award.

Diungkapkan bahwa the plot kicks in after misty gets a call from her brother donny (paul sparks), forcing her to reckon with her nashville past. He wants Misty to find her. His daughter, rising country star Charlie Hart (Carter Faith), has gone missing. I guess a musician is better equipped to find missing people than the Nashville police? I don’t know, but let’s just roll with it.

Diungkapkan bahwa misty embarks on a road trip back home to look into the case, getting in touch with the most important people in charlie’s life, including her manager (garrett hedlund), her rude boyfriend jace jacobs (singer ross lynch), and her publicity team. Misty finds that no one cares for Charlie; they were all just using her for her to sell albums and tickets. She also uncovers a conspiracy that grows more and more tangled with every passing scene.

Diungkapkan bahwa in heartland, nashville is depicted as a kind of rural gotham, hiding corruption and schemes on every corner. “And you and me? We ain’t famous anymore. The film makes it clear that Misty is not welcome and the more she probes, the bigger the target on her back becomes. “Nashville’s changed,” warns one of Jones’ old friends. ” Okay?.

Diungkapkan bahwa there aren’t many surprises in heartland, with charlie’s disappearance resolved in a twist you can see coming the minute misty has her first drink in nashville. Still, the film boasts a surprisingly talented cast, ranging from Sparks, who’s reduced to phone call scenes where he’s nagging at Misty, to Chastain herself.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the oscar-winning actress is fully committed to the part, looking more and more haggard as the film progresses. She gets dragged onstage several times, resulting in some fun numbers that mix original music and covers. Chastain does her own singing, holding her own alongside real-life performers. Winnie Jo Lean (Jennifer Nettles, from the musical duo Sugarland) joins Misty onstage to perform the film’s official song, called, you guessed it, “Heartland. Charlie’s boyfriend Jace Jacobs invites Misty onstage to intimidate her, only for the crowd to be swept off their feet by the unexpected comeback of a retired country superstar. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, other noteworthy performers include hedlund, who’d previously worked with feste in country strong, and an inexplicable cameo from john hawkes as misty’s former husband clark. As always, Hawkes is electric onscreen, but he’s featured in one scene.

Berdasarkan laporan, i can imagine a better version of this movie, one that goes all in on its strange fusion of genres. Instead, Heartland is formulaic, with nothing new to say about the music industry or the perils of being a young woman in it. It’s for die-hard Chastain fans, or something to play in the background if you love a mild-mannered train wreck.

Berdasarkan laporan, amid calls for reparations, there are questions about the future of the commonwealth and who its next head should be. In conversation with Vanity Fair, constitutional expert Ed Owens, author of After Elizabeth: Can the Monarchy Save Itself?, discusses what’s in store for the future.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

King Charles reacts near Antigua and Barbuda flags during a visit to Nelson's Dockyard, a historic naval base established in 1725, during his visit to Antigua and Barbuda on November 2, 2026 in St John's, Antigua and Barbuda.

Vanity Fair: Prince William has made it clear that he does not necessarily expect to follow his father as head of the Commonwealth, saying that the decision belongs to the Commonwealth itself.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, ed owens: prince william hinted after his difficult 2022 tour of belize, the bahamas, and jamaica that he wasn’t focused on following his father as head of the commonwealth. King Charles got the role because his mother and predecessor, Queen Elizabeth II, actively lobbied Commonwealth heads of state to ensure that the role would pass to him when he became monarch, following her death. Crucially, the position of head of the Commonwealth is not hereditary. A couple of weeks ago The Times of London confirmed that the prince’s position was unchanged on this issue. But it will not automatically transfer to William when Charles dies.

What is the Commonwealth and how significant is that statement?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the commonwealth of nations (as it’s officially known) is a voluntary association of 56 independent member states. Most of these member states were once colonies in the British empire. Decolonization began after World War II and most newly independent states—though no longer part of the empire—became part of the new Commonwealth. This new international body represented change but also continuity, enabling Britain to maintain a global (but mostly symbolic) presence at a time when its real geopolitical power was rapidly in retreat. George VI was the last emperor and first Head of the Commonwealth. The Commonwealth also provided a stage for the monarchy to continue to exercise an important international role. The latter role was invented by the British government to replace the former and allowed the monarch to maintain a semblance of global prestige while helping to facilitate the process of decolonization.

Berdasarkan laporan, although most member states have historical ties to britain, any country can apply to join the commonwealth—exemplified by recent members like rwanda, mozambique, gabon, and togo. Members commit to shared principles outlined in the Commonwealth charter, including democracy, human rights, the rule of law, and sustainable development. In reality, though, many member states have failed to live up to these principles, and the Commonwealth has, in recent years, felt morally directionless.

Diungkapkan bahwa william’s reluctance to take on the mantle of head of the commonwealth isn’t that surprising: he and his advisers want to future-proof his reign. One way to do this is to identify potential problems in order to avoid them. The Commonwealth is one such potential problem, and William seems to have calculated that the headship of this organization likely represents more trouble than it is worth.

Does it represent a fundamental shift in the monarchy’s attitude toward the organization, or simply an acknowledgement that the old imperial relationship is no longer sustainable?.

Sebagaimana diketahui, we have to remember that 15 members of the commonwealth (including the uk) are also “realms”—i. Indeed, we can even interpret the tour as the king and his courtiers preparing the ground for this transition to republics. Eventually all 14 nations, and perhaps the UK too, will opt to become republics, cutting their ties with the crown. I think it’s clear even to the current king that his position as monarch of the 14 realms beyond Britain is unsustainable. e. their head of state is King Charles. Those nations most likely to become republics soonest—owing to the fact that they have surging republican movements—are the Caribbean realms, two of which (the Bahamas and Antigua and Barbuda) King Charles visited during his recent tour to the Caribbean. This is because, though former realms will no longer have as their head of state the incumbent monarch, they will almost certainly remain members of the wider Commonwealth.

Sebagaimana diketahui, what king charles was trying to do with his latest tour was to inject energy and meaning into the idea of the commonwealth, more than attempt to reinvigorate the personal bonds that connect him to his peoples in the caribbean. In loudly acknowledging the injustices of the slave trade in which Britain was, for a long time, complicit, while also reminding his hosts that Britain was one of the first major powers to abolish and oppose slavery—the king has sought to address and ease concerns in ways that might enable the Commonwealth to function more cohesively in the future, irrespective of whether the UK’s monarch remains in post as head of the Commonwealth.

When Charles eventually leaves the throne, could the Commonwealth decide that it no longer needs a British monarch as its figurehead? What might replace that role? Will the Commonwealth continue?.

Berdasarkan laporan, i absolutely think [the] commonwealth nations will look to replace the british monarch with a new figurehead. My sense is that many nations would already prefer to have a different kind of figurehead, for example a head who belongs to one of the 56 member states and is elected by member states for a set term. Alternatively, there could be some kind of “rolling” headship, whereby every member nation is invited to elect an official who will take a 12-month turn as head of the Commonwealth.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, whether or not the commonwealth will continue is more difficult to say. Certainly one of the reasons it has survived until now is because of the energy and engagement of two British monarchs—Charles and Elizabeth II—who have viewed it as a potential force for good in the world. Without its connection to the British monarchy, it may lose what is left of its momentum. However, its survival also depends on wider geopolitical shifts: If individual governments within the Commonwealth view it as [a] useful arena for bringing together states who could benefit from closer association—be that economic, political, or military association—then it may continue long into the future.

Berdasarkan laporan, there is an increasingly difficult conversation about britain’s colonial past, slavery, and reparations. Charles has expressed personal sorrow over the slave trade, but the question of a formal apology remains politically and constitutionally complicated. How much freedom does the king actually have to address these issues, and could William take a different approach?.

Berdasarkan laporan, the king has very little freedom to apologize unless his government specifically sanctions and encourages such an apology. As the recent Caribbean tour made clear, I think Charles would prefer to strike a more nuanced line, reminding audiences that, despite the UK’s colonial past and its involvement in the horrors of slavery, Britain was one of the first major powers to abolish slavery and that it played an important role in bringing to an end the maritime trade in human chattel. Whether William takes a different approach will depend entirely on the UK government’s approach to formal apologies and reparations. My sense is that no government—at least not now or in the near-to-medium-term future—will agree to financial reparations, because historians, philosophers, and politicians are increasingly pushing back on such a solution, questioning why UK taxpayers (already under huge strain) should fork out huge sums for the wrongs committed by some of their ancestors more than two centuries ago.

What would Queen Elizabeth II make of this? She saw the Commonwealth as her father’s legacy and her second family.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i think she would probably be relatively relaxed, recognizing that times change and institutions have to evolve. William has decided that given the challenges and changes of the mid-20th century the monarchy and royal family’s future is likely to be stronger without the post-imperial baggage of the Commonwealth. Let’s not forget that as queen she oversaw many key alterations in the way both the monarchy and Commonwealth functioned through her long reign, as was required by shifts in politics, economics, culture, and social norms. While the Commonwealth was of emotional importance to her—not least for the way it connected her back to her father and predecessors—by the end of her reign it was already a shadow of what it once had been and she would have known that it was likely to continue on a trajectory of decline. I think his grandmother would have respected the way he is putting the family firm first in this instance.

Jude Bellingham, star of England’s men’s soccer team and Real Madrid, admitted his skills are limited to the pitch, and that he hasn’t yet learned how to drive or cook.

Jude Bellingham may be one of the greatest footballers of his generation.

But as it turns out, Team England’s star midfielder’s basic everyday skills—or lack thereof—help level the playing field, bringing him closer to us mere mortals.

Berdasarkan laporan, “there’s loads of things i don’t know how to do,” bellingham told british vogue in an interview published nov. 10. I’m good at what I do, but everything else? Not that great. “I can’t cook, I can’t drive. I rely on my friends, my family to help me do stuff—chef, cleaner, mum, whoever else. That’s where I’m at. ”.

In fact, he’s been so busy keeping his eye on the literal ball—and doing a really good job at it—he may have lost track of life’s other skills.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i work hard every day and all day, and then when i get home,” the 23-year-old said, “i’ve probably neglected learning how to do some of the more basic things. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, but, as he noted, “there’ll be a time and a place for that, i’m sure. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “the world cup, for me, was probably the best experience i’ve had in my life, full stop,” the real madrid player said. “While I was in it, I really made the conscious decision to enjoy this. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, after all, “it doesn’t come around very often,” he added. “It’s rare. ”.

And while Bellingham’s World Cup performance won him fans around the world—as did his endearing bromance with former Borussia Dortmund teammate and Norway’s star Erling Haaland—nowhere was more grateful for his performance than England.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, as he noted, “i’ve seen a lot of people say, ‘i don’t think i’ve ever had a night when i was so happy and so proud to be english. ’”.

#215. The Role of the “Queen Mother” in Monarchies Around the World: Queen Sofía, Sonia of Norway, and Beatrix of the Netherlands

📅 10 Nov 2026

The Role of the “Queen Mother” in Monarchies Around the World: Queen Sofía, Sonia of Norway, and Beatrix of the Netherlands

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.vanityfair.com/story/queen-mother-around-the-world

Berdasarkan laporan, queen sofía celebrated her 88th birthday on november 2 and remains a pillar of the spanish royal family, with a demanding schedule that includes at least one official engagement per week. Queen Sofía has never set aside her institutional role, unlike some other European “queen mothers” (this official title is used only in the United Kingdom but is commonly used to refer to the mothers of kings), who, to a greater or lesser extent, continue to work for the monarchy in their respective countries.

Berdasarkan laporan, this week, queen sofía will be in san fernando, cádiz, where she will serve as patroness of the ceremony to present the national ensign to the marine corps, a special unit within the navy and the world’s oldest marine corps, created in 1537 by emperor charles i. Far from retiring from public life, the Queen Emerita continues to play an important role within the Crown; she retains her office at Zarzuela and receives an official stipend.

Sebagaimana diketahui, she also remains closely involved in the day-to-day activities of the queen sofía foundation and regularly visits the provincial offices of the spanish federation of food banks to learn about its charitable work, among other projects. Always discreet, Felipe VI’s mother has weathered the controversies surrounding Juan Carlos and maintained a professional image dedicated to serving the Spanish people—one that her family circumstances have not tarnished.

Queen Sonja, a great source of support today for her son, King Haakon.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, following the death of her husband, king harald, in late august, and with the newly crowned queen mette-marit on medical leave, queen sonja of norway has become a pillar of support for her son, haakon viii. Sonia of Norway is 89 years old and in recent months has had minor health scares that led to her being hospitalized for a few days in the hospital. But despite everything, she continues her duties as a member of the Norwegian royal family. Just a few days ago, Queen Sonja traveled to Málaga to attend the opening of an exhibition on Picasso and Munch at the Picasso Museum in the Andalusian city, and was all smiles during a visit to a Norwegian school in Benalmádena.

Diungkapkan bahwa on november 3, queen sonja accompanied her son haakon to an official dinner to welcome the provincial governors at the royal palace—an important event at which the king will have his mother’s support in the absence of his wife and his daughter, crown princess ingrid alexandra, who is currently focused on her university studies in oslo. Two days later, Queen Sonja will visit the Furniture Maker School in Askim, attend the opening of a furniture exhibition at the Center for Democracy at Fort Høytorp, and meet with members of the Indre Østfold Women’s Group and young people at the Re:læx youth center in Askim.

Berdasarkan laporan, after more than three decades as queen, sonia of norway has stayed by her son’s side, at a time when he needs her support more than ever. Since her accession to the throne, Queen Sonia—whom Haakon stripped of the title “Her Majesty,” now simply Queen Sonia—has become a cornerstone of institutional and family support for the new monarch.

Beatrix of the Netherlands served as queen for 33 years.

Berdasarkan laporan, at 88 years old, beatrix of the netherlands does not have a schedule as busy as those of queen sofía or queen sonja of norway, but she has continued to attend institutional events and fulfill some official engagements since her abdication in 2013. King Willem-Alexander’s mother actively participates in award ceremonies linked to the Crown, such as the Appeltjes van Oranje awards presented by the Oranje Fonds foundation—awards whose bronze statuettes she designed herself and which she attends each year alongside King Willem-Alexander and Queen Máxima.

Berdasarkan laporan, in addition, princess beatrix continues to make official trips to the dutch caribbean territories (such as her recent visits to bonaire, st. Eustatius, and Saba) to preside over events dedicated to nature conservation, sustainable development, and education. She also continues to attend certain cultural and charitable events in her home country, such as the Dutch Ballet Gala hosted by the Dansersfonds Foundation, which she attended in mid-October.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, beatrix of the netherlands, who now resides at drakenstein castle, was queen of the netherlands for 33 years, from 1980 to 2013. Following the coronation of her son Willem, she regained the title of princess, and today her official title is Her Royal Highness Princess Beatrix of the Netherlands, Princess of Orange-Nassau, and Princess of Lippe-Biesterfeld. Beatrix of the Netherlands remains deeply loved and respected by the people, and within the Orange-Nassau royal family, she continues to support and guide her son, King Willem-Alexander.

Princess Beatrix is a great role model for her granddaughter, Princess Amalia.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, queen sofía, queen sonja of norway, and beatrix of the netherlands all embody the key institutional values essential to preserving the monarchy in their respective countries. Loyal to the crown in one capacity or another and having dedicated their lives to public service for decades, all three are great examples of institutional loyalty for their granddaughters— Princess Leonor, Princess Ingrid Alexandra, and Princess Amalia—who will one day become queens.

Sports Reporter Julie Stewart-Binks is delivering an empowering message to her fans about being laid off by regional sports network SNY weeks after undergoing skin cancer treatment.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “your job and your workplace is not your identity and don’t you ever forget that,” stewart-binks, 39, insisted via a tuesday, november 10, instagram reel. “Don’t give them the power over who you are. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “this particular layoff happened friday at sny,” stewart-binks confirmed. “This is a place I’ve been a contributor as a host, reporter, and opinionist for the last seven years. While it affects me, hundreds of other people have been affected more — I see you all and I empathize deeply with having your livelihood ripped away from you. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, she continued, “i’ve been through this song and dance in many different ways. Rather than pretending I’m amazing, that nothing is wrong with me, and that life is always perfect (one of the big reasons this app sucks) I know my journey here is about being honest, vulnerable, and saying the quiet part out loud (trying to make your time on here make you feel less like crap). ”.

Stewart-Binks recalled feeling a range of emotions after finding out she’d lost her job via a New York Times article about the layoffs.

Sebagaimana diketahui, “in all honesty, it really sucks for a lot of people,” she acknowledged. ‘It’s just part of the business. ’ But it turns out, part of the business is wondering how many American holidays you have to work to be invited to the holiday party until you get a message from your former agent that says FYI and it’s a link to a New York Times article where it says you don’t have a job anymore. “In sports broadcasting, we spend most of our time talking about this, athletes being cut, waived, released. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa the journalist likened the sports media landscape to a game of “musical chairs [where] someone keeps taking the chairs away mid-song. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, despite her personal career setback, stewart-binks pointed out that being laid off is “more common than we think. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “there’s no one right way to navigate what comes next,” she noted. “If you’re in this chapter too, I see you. ”.

When the job cuts were announced earlier this week, a SNY spokesperson told the New York Times that the network is undergoing structural and programming changes.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “as part of our regular review of our business, operations and programming, sny has decided to cease broadcasting baseball night in new york and sportsnite,” a sny statement read. Ongoing coverage of the Mets and New York sports are at the heart of SNY’s business, and we remain focused on continuing to deliver high-quality content to our passionate fans. “We are grateful to those team members that helped bring these programs to fans for many years. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, meanwhile, stewart-binks explained a recent onair absence in october by sharing that she’d undergone “a mohs surgery to remove squamous cell carcinoma from my nose. ” The procedure removes thin layers of skin in hopes of eliminating cancerous cells without disrupting healthy skin around it, per the Mayo Clinic.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i thought it was a pimple that wouldn’t go away, turns out it was cancer,” she tweeted on october 7. “I share this so that hopefully it inspires others to get checked if something feels/looks off. ”.

The TV host disclosed that her surgeon “grafted part of my ear” onto her nose as part of the Mohs operation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “i’ve played hockey my entire life, but never felt more like a hockey player than i do now. Sew me up and put me in coach,” she joked.

Aside from her work with SNY, Stewart-Binks covered the Milan Cortina Winter Olympics for the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation in February, in addition to reporting for Barstool, TNT, ESPN and Fox Sports.

Why do I have to be dressed the same as him?’” he recalled. You know, I’m the older brother. Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, i didn’t think there was any way survivor 51 could outcrazy that wild tribal council confrontation between kilby, lewis, sharonda, eric, cristian and linnea a few weeks ago where two extra votes were played and they all threatened to draw rocks. I was wrong. Last night’s Double Duos twist may have outcrazied that mess, as we got an idol play, two shots in the dark and maybe the weirdest extra vote decision in the history of Survivor. Wrong. It’s that last part I’m particularly fascinated by, as I’ve watched the episode twice and am still baffled by the decision-making. I’m not the only one either.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, let’s walk through this step by step because there’s a lot going on here. If you play your shot in the dark on Survivor, which gives you a 1 in 6 chance of drawing a scroll that keeps you safe, you lose your ability to vote. Cristian was picked to go on the journey and earned an extra vote that was only good for that night’s Tribal Council. With all the chaos and uncertainty at Tribal Council, however, he and Carter, who were paired as a duo, decided Cristian should play his shot in the dark to try and earn safety for the pair. That meant Cristian couldn’t use the extra vote himself and needed to give it away to someone else.

Berdasarkan laporan, cristian has a lot of close allies and is a member of the so-called salt alliance, but for unclear reasons, he decided to give the vote to eric, who is not part of the alliance, during tribal council. He told Eric he was giving him the vote to build trust, and since they do have some history together on a shared pre-merge tribe, he may have thought that was the best way to ensure Eric would vote with them. Now, you might be thinking this is the baffling Tribal Council decision I referenced in the headline, but it’s not. I think it was a weird move, but I sort of understand where Cristian was coming from. Personally, I would have just had Carter play the vote, but I can kind of, sort of see where he was coming from.

Berdasarkan laporan, no, the baffling decision was what eric then did with that vote. He just put it in his pocket and noped out, despite the fact that he knew it was only good for that night’s Tribal Council. In his voting confessional, he said he didn’t think it needed to be played since he thought they had the numbers on their side. So, he just… didn’t play it and let it expire without ever being used.

Diungkapkan bahwa i was so confused during my first viewing that i thought i must have misheard the television. Nope. He just didn’t play it because he thought the votes were already there. I did not. Not surprisingly, fans on social media were collectively confused as well. I saw numerous tweets trying to work out the why and even former players calling out his bizarre decision.

Berdasarkan laporan, now, to be clear, i’m not saying there’s an obvious play eric should have made with the extra vote. He could have thrown a random vote on Mike and Maggie to help protect himself and Thien An in case they caught their own stray vote. He could have simply thrown it on Jelly and Dev to solidify that trust with Cristian. Either of those paths would have been perfectly fine, but instead, he did nothing with it and opened himself up to possible problems with Cristian.

Diungkapkan bahwa everyone knows how many votes were cast last night. Maybe they make it a thing. Maybe they don’t. They can all count; so, in theory, Cristian and Carter should be able to figure out that Eric just put the extra vote in his pocket. Either way, it seems like a wild gamble to take when the vote has no practical value and at least Cristian and Carter and perhaps more players in that alliance can call him out later if he tries to pretend like it’s a real vote as a leverage move later in the game.

Diungkapkan bahwa i can’t wait to get a full explanation from eric whenever he does pregame press about why he didn’t use the extra vote. In a perfect world, we'll even get a confessional about it in the edit next week. Regardless of his reasons though, his decision will go down as yet another example of why this season of Survivor has been the best in a long time, at least so far. The scheming is incessant, and production has mostly found the right balance between twists and getting out of the way. The castaways are all over the top and ridiculous. I can’t wait to see how it all concludes.

Paapa Essiedu, Harry Potter’s New Snape, Is Ready for Questions

Tanggal: 10 Nov 2026 | Sumber: https://www.vanityfair.com/story/paapa-essiedu-interview

Berdasarkan laporan, when paapa essiedu was just 25 years old, he was cast as hamlet by the royal shakespeare company. “I still remember the day that my agent rang me up and told me I’d got that job,” he says 11 years later. In an instant, he joined the ranks of all-time greats like Ben Kingsley, Kenneth Branagh, and Mark Rylance. “I was gassed about it for about three seconds. And then I was like, ‘Fuck, what have I done?’”.

Diungkapkan bahwa critics loved essiedu as the danish prince. Yet his casting provoked headlines for another reason: He was the first Black actor to play Hamlet at the RSC. “It was good,” he says casually of his star-making performance. “There was this—not even fascination—this obsession with the fact that I was a Black person who was doing it,” he recalls.

Berdasarkan laporan, the olivier-winning, emmy-nominated performer now views that stint as a dry run for the most high-profile role of his career: potions professor severus snape in hbo’s highly anticipated and deeply polarizing harry potter television series. “I kind of draw a small pathway in comparison to the freeway that I’m on now,” he says.

Berdasarkan laporan, there is likely not a soul alive who isn’t familiar with j. After seven primary books, a variety of secondary volumes, eight feature films, multiple spin-offs, a Broadway play, and rides and shops at six Universal theme parks worldwide, Harry Potter arguably has name recognition rivaling that of Hamlet, or Jesus. “On the record, I’m not agreeing with this here, just in case. Rowling’s multibillion-dollar franchise about a boy wizard. ” He flicks his wrist. K. “Trust me, she can shut down the whole of Vanity Fair like that. Though “don’t let my auntie hear you comparing Harry Potter to the Bible,” says Essiedu. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, essiedu was raised in the east london neighborhood of walthamstow by his mother, who never imagined her son might have a career as a professional actor. “It was not on the top-five list of jobs that were made available. ” His father, who lived back in Ghana with Essiedu’s half-siblings, died when Essiedu was 14. “Single Ghanaian woman parent?” he says. “He was there, but he wasn’t there,” Essiedu says.

Diungkapkan bahwa the 36-year-old describes his childhood as “fully millennial”: “slap-bang in the middle, pre-internet, pre-fucking-netflix, on-demand television, just barely dealing with game boy colors. But while many his age are predisposed to wax poetic about life in the ’90s, Essiedu doesn’t see it with entirely rose-colored glasses. Life was analog,” he says. “There was a lot of just staring out the window and hoping some shit was going to happen. “In many ways, it was fucking boring,” he says with a laugh. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, reading became “something that was quite crucial to stop me from eating my own hands,” he says—including the harry potter books, which “were coming out regularly at the precise time that i was starting to develop my taste for literature…. I’m like, ‘I’m going home. I’m inside. The world that was created was so full. Can you imagine, like, 12-year-old boys, 13-year-old boys reading 600-page books, 700-page books about wizards? We’re meant to be out here in the streets playing football, basketball, whatever. I’m reading the book. ’”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, all grown up “they’re considering me for a teacher. That means I’m fucking old now," says Essiedu. They’re just old. "When you’re a kid, teachers don’t even have ages. ".

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, when he was 18, essiedu joined the national youth theatre—a selective performing arts training center in london where actors like daniel day-lewis, helen mirren, and daniel craig honed their craft. After getting accepted, Essiedu raised the money he needed to attend, going around his school asking friends and acquaintances for donations. Essiedu auditioned for a distinctly teenage reason: “Let’s just say there was someone that I wanted to be around who was also going to National Youth Theatre,” he says cheekily. The crush might not have lasted—“let’s say the person who I was supposedly following disappeared”—but a lifelong passion for performing developed.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i found myself just in this room surrounded by people who were talking about shakespeare and talking about harold pinter and jez butterworth,” he says. “By luck, really, I found myself in a room that gave me the idea to basically burn down all of my mother’s ambitions for myself and go in a different direction. Arguably, it turned out okay. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, after his star turn as hamlet, essiedu got an emmy nomination for his supporting role in michaela coel’s i may destroy you. “I think it was a phenomenally singular and confident and brave and unprecedented piece of work. He wasn’t surprised when the show made a recent New York Times list of 100 best TV shows of the 21st century: “Of course it was on that list,” he says. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa then francesca gardiner and mark mylod—a pair of emmy-winning succession alums—reached out to let him know they were interested in him for the new harry potter. Snape was the only part he wanted, though the role was a bit of a reality check: “They’re considering me for a teacher. When you’re a kid, teachers don’t even have ages. That means I’m fucking old now. They’re just old. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa good news “i got a lot of love as well," he says. "That really fuels me as much as the hate. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa essiedu put his pride aside and met with gardiner and mylod. “He has to be intimidating, dangerous, sometimes very funny, but there’s also an enormous amount that he’s concealing. “Professor Snape requires an extraordinary actor,” Gardiner tells VF via email. Someone who can convey depth and complexity without necessarily saying a word. Much to his surprise, after a two-hour chat about the show, Essiedu found out he had the part. You need someone who can make you feel that there’s a whole other story unfolding beneath the one you’re watching. Paapa is one of those rare actors who can do all of that. Someone with real intensity. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa acting stalwart john lithgow stars opposite essiedu as hogwarts headmaster albus dumbledore. “He is so focused and intense, and yet there’s an ease to his acting,” says Lithgow. Over the phone, the veteran says he’s never acted with anyone quite like Essiedu. “He just has a great sense of how mysterious he is, which is what makes him so compelling as Snape in Harry Potter. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, “we simply needed one of the greatest actors in britain to do it justice,” agrees mylod, also via email. Essiedu “has extraordinary range, and I always, always believe him. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, in april 2025, hbo announced that essiedu had won the role of snape—played with an inimitable snarl in the film franchise by the late great alan rickman. “I still don’t think I really know what happens in Deathly Hallows because I read it so quickly that it didn’t really seep in. I was like, ‘This shit is complicated as hell, man. “To be honest, I never watched the movies when I was younger,” he says. Essiedu read the books to prepare, but opted not to watch the movies. Dumbledore’s dead? What the fuck?’”.

Berdasarkan laporan, but even if he only has passing familiarity with rickman’s take on the character, essiedu says he’s not focused on trying to reinvent snape or make people forget about his predecessor’s work. He’s a legend,” Essiedu says of Rickman. “The guy is an icon. There’s so much goodwill, and I really feel him with me. “Anyone who’s ever met Alan or spoken to him or been friends with him have all reached out to me and spoken about what Alan would’ve thought about my casting. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, the public’s reaction was decidedly more complex. After Essiedu’s casting was announced, the internet erupted, with certain corners deeply upset that a Black man was stepping into the role. In March, Essiedu told The Times of London that he’d received death threats from so-called Harry Potter fans: “Quit or I’ll murder you,” one said.

Diungkapkan bahwa essiedu doesn’t have a problem with good-faith criticism. “Then there are the people who are like, ‘You are bad because you are Black’—which, to me, is racist. “Well, actually not ‘You’re bad because you are Black. ” He stops to reconsider his words for a moment. “There’s some people who are just like, ‘I’ve done my research, and I know what kind of actor you are, and you suck. ’ But there is a racially driven animosity. ’ And they’re totally entitled to their opinion,” he says. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, in the final weeks before the series premiere, though, essiedu is most concerned with a third group, one he has real empathy for. After this, we’re not going to burn the books. We’re not going to remove the DVDs of the films. That all still exists. It’s not the end of that. I’m not trying to break anybody’s nothing. “There are people who have got such a tight and deeply felt connection to something that they believe is theirs, and it feels like somebody is trying to take their thing and break their thing,” he says. Essiedu has a message for that cohort: “I know that’s not what I’m trying to do. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, and essiedu is quick to point out that the vitriol hasn’t been universal: “i got a lot of love as well,” he says. “That really fuels me as much as the hate. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, he’s also aware that he could avoid much of the bad stuff by staying offline—if only it were that easy. “You’ve got your DMs, and then there’s the bit where it says ‘request’ or ‘hidden,’” he says. But you can’t stop yourself from doing it. “You know you shouldn’t go in there. You know you don’t need to scratch that itch. You want to know what the face of the monster looks like. ”.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, essiedu’s showrunner, at least, has his back. Paapa has absolutely nailed the role, and it is that performance that deserves our attention. “He has handled it with incredible grace, and I have nothing but the greatest respect for him…. “It’s appalling that anyone should be subjected to that kind of abuse in any circumstances,” writes Gardiner. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, although i've been sworn to secrecy, it seems to me that the only major difference between the harry potter from yore and the new series is essiedu’s casting. Though the plot unfolds more slowly—the show has approximately eight hours to fill, after all, rather than two—the world of the series looks more or less the same as the one in the original films, from Hogwarts to Diagon Alley to the Dursleys’ house. Dominic McLaughlin, Arabella Stanton, and Alastair Stout, who play Harry, Hermione, and Ron, respectively, bear a striking resemblance to their forebears, Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson, and Rupert Grint—particularly McLaughlin. In this milieu, Essiedu’s dreadlocked Snape stands out—which has potentially given the trolls more ammo.

Essiedu as Professor Snape in Harry Potter on HBO.

Sebagaimana diketahui, essiedu says he’s “very clear-minded in my head about what i want to do and what i’m trying to achieve, and the potential of it. And you can judge me sometime—in 2039 or whatever it is—as to whether it’s been successful or not. ” Having more time to tell the story means “hopefully I get the opportunity to pull the contradictions and the unexpected masks of Severus so that eventually we get a human being that is fully fleshed [out] and living and breathing. That was my ambition, and is my ambition. ”.

Diungkapkan bahwa there’s another reason one might have some trepidation about joining the staff of hogwarts at this particular moment. While Rowling is adamant that she is not anti-trans, some, like The Matrix director Lilly Wachowski, have said that anyone who supports the Harry Potter franchise is “supporting trans genocide. Rowling—the mastermind behind Harry Potter—has descended into what her critics characterize as anti-transgender activism, using her apparently endless supply of cash to support gender-essentialist policies in the UK. In the past decade, J. K. ”.

Sebagaimana diketahui, shortly after he was cast in the series, essiedu signed an open letter in support of the transgender, nonbinary, and intersex community. Rowling then made a post on X saying that she does not have the power to fire him from the show—but wouldn’t even if she could.

Diungkapkan bahwa “i have been super clear about my position on this topic, and that is the reason why she spoke out about me,” says essiedu. I can only be really, really clear about what I believe and be consistent with that. I’m not really here to speak about Jo’s politics or to be a mouthpiece for her. “I’m really keen not to make a kind of ‘them and us’ dynamic here. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, so, what does he believe? after a bit of equivocating (“i don’t want to talk about jo at all,” he repeats), essiedu says the following with his chest: “i believe, in my bones, that trans people, queer people, people of all creeds and color have got the right to be treated with respect and dignity and safety at all times—whether they’re in the workplace, whether they’re at home or in the street, whatever. That’s the creed by which I live. That’s what I believe, and that’s the way that I choose to live my life. ”.

Berdasarkan laporan, perhaps that statement presents an inherent contradiction. Rowling is actively involved with the new series and will generate income from it that she could then use to fund her pet causes. But Essiedu believes Rowling’s books—rather than her politics—prove why it’s important to tell Harry’s story again for a new generation.

Dalam perkembangan terbarunya, “when i come back to this story—this actual story—i’m thinking about the themes that it explores,” he says. “Themes of forgiveness, and good triumphing over evil, and of accepting people for who they are and allowing people to really be themselves within a world where anything is possible. #234. Sonia Gandhi Gives an Intimate Account of Her Husband Rajiv Gandhi’s Final Days and Assassination
